title: Wasm-WCET: Worst-Case Execution-Time Analysis of WebAssembly Modules on Updatable Resource-Constrained Embedded Devices
Authors: M. Seidler; M. Michelis; P. Wägemann; R. Kapitza
Author Affiliations: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 32nd Real-Time and Embedded Technology and Applications Symposium (RTAS)
Abstract: Updating programmable logic controllers (PLCs) is mostly reserved for their manufacturers (i.e., original equipment manufacturers, OEMs), as modifications to the underlying software may jeopardize system integrity and safety. Consequently, operators of manufacturing systems remain reliant on OEMs for ongoing support, particularly as systems often operate for 25 years or longer. WebAssembly (Wasm), a portable bytecode format, is well-suited to enabling controlled software updates thanks to its spatial isolation, which could give operators greater freedom to adapt their systems. However, temporal isolation remains unaddressed so far. Moreover, using a portable bytecode prevents the application of typical two-stage (i.e., path and hardware) worst-case execution-time (WCET) analysis to ensure timing protection, as the binary is no longer executed directly on the hardware. Instead, the interpreter introduces an additional layer of control flow, including unbounded loops—even for fundamental instructions. Moreover, gaining independence from OEMs requires minimal system interweaving, whereas OEMs must preserve trust in their initial safety mechanisms and their integrity. Finally, PLCs are usually highly resource-constrained.With our Wasm-WCET framework, we provide the first WCET analysis for Wasm designed to be conducted on the resource-constrained device, thereby reducing system interweaving and improving updatability. We integrate a third stage to the WCET analysis and develop the first interpreter cost model for Wasm bytecode. Additionally, we incorporate a specialization prior to analysis to manage unbounded loops in the interpreter’s path component, thereby reducing overestimation by up to 98%. We implement a timing-schema–based prototype and present a memory-efficient in-place analysis leveraging Wasm’s structured control flow. Our prototype implementation yields results on a microcontroller with 128KiB of RAM in under 27ms.
Author Keywords: WebAssembly (Wasm);worst-case execution time (WCET);static analysis;real-time systems

title: TimeProbe: A Measurement-Based Probabilistic Timing Analysis Tool
Authors: V. H. Sahin

Abstract: Timing analysis is a crucial aspect of real-time systems, a type of computer system with timing constraints. Before a real-time system is deployed, developers must convince the certification authorities that the system meets its deadlines. To achieve this, they perform a worst-case execution time analysis (WCET) of the real-time programs. One of the WCET analysis approaches is the measurement-based probabilistic timing analysis (MBPTA), which is based on measuring the execution times of real-time programs in an experimental setup and fitting a probability distribution that represents WCETs of the programs. One method used during the fitting operation is the extreme value theory (EVT). This paper outlines the mathematical framework underlying MBPTA in the context of the EVT; presents one way to apply MBPTA using the Block Maxima (BM) method, Method of L-Moments (MoLM), and quantile-quantile plot (Q-Q plot) method; and introduces an open-source WCET analysis tool, namely TimeProbe, that uses the presented approach.

Abstract: We present a Python based API, software components, and reference system for safely running machine learning models alongside an F Prime flight software binary. Abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) systems enable an alternative form of human-computer interaction that does not rely on conventional input devices by transforming neural signals into control commands. In this study, a real-time electroencephalography EEG control system based on eye-blink detection was designed and implemented using the OpenBCI platform. To improve the reliability of baseline amplitude-threshold detection, a simple yet effective optimized detection strategy was introduced. Frontal EEG signals were streamed in real time using the Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) and processed in a Python environment. Our proposed method reduces false detections by combining adaptive threshold values based on resting state statistics and eye blink duration constraints, instead of relying directly on signal amplitude. The detected eye-blink events were mapped to standard keyboard commands to control presentation slides in real time. This approach demonstrates the potential to extend the same interface to other control applications, such as scrolling web-based content. Experiments were conducted with a single participant, and the results indicate that the proposed optimized method substantially reduces false positives compared to the baseline amplitude-threshold approach while maintaining stable performance required for real-time control. The results show that combining a low-cost EEG device with a lightweight and efficient optimized detection algorithm enables its use in assistive technologies and widely used interactive systems. This provides a practical foundation for implementing real-time human-computer interfaces.

Abstract: Recognizing algorithmically equivalent code written in different programming languages remains a fundamental challenge in multi-language introductory programming courses. Two programs representing the same algorithm using two different languages—in one case, C and another case, Java—create disjoint syntax trees such that matching tokenization algorithms will not detect algorithmic equivalence between languages. Neural embedding approaches achieve cross-language representation but require labeled fine-tuning corpora unavailable in labeled-data-scarce CS-1 settings, and produce dense vectors that cannot enumerate which algorithmic patterns a submission contains—a capability essential for interpretable instructional feedback. This paper proposes a deterministic, gradient-free framework for cross-language algorithmic similarity in CS-1 educational settings, covering C, C++, and Java. Context Normalization Protocol—a cross-language label unification process applied to Code Property Graph (CPG) nodes—our framework makes it possible to perform direct comparisons between patterns irrespective of language without any form of learned alignment. An extended 21-pattern Computation Evolution Signatures (CES) taxonomy, comprising pattern-level descriptors of variable evolution within loops and recursive calls, covers CS-1 imperative strategies across all three languages. An asymmetrical Tversky formulation compensates for Java’s innate verbosity by assigning a low weight to irrelevant patterns submitted by the students while retaining the ability to capture necessary reference strategies. The framework is able to enumerate the algorithmic patterns present in every submitted code without using GPUs and labeled fine-tuning data. Under matched held-out evaluation, the model attains 88.75% top-1 recall accuracy, whereas the neural baseline achieves 71.37%, highlighting the model’s effectiveness in scenarios where labeled data for fine-tuning is lacking. On the entire 400-program cross-language evaluation task, the aggregate cross-language retrieval accuracy is 87.25% ( $349/400$ , all directions), with the core directions (Java→C/C++ and C $\leftrightarrow $ C++) reaching 88.60% ( $342/386$ ). The Java→C/C++ cross-frontend direction, which constitutes 35% of evaluation pairs, attains 91.43% ( $128/140$ ). The remaining 61.5% of pairs share the C/C++ parser frontend. The aggregate performance is primarily driven by the Java→C/C++ and C $\leftrightarrow $ C++ directions; the remaining sparse directions are detailed in Section VI-B, indicating that the aggregate score does not imply symmetric cross-language performance. Feature weights are estimated using only monolingual C code without retraining ( $p{\lt }0.0001$  compared to a lexical BL-view ablation). All findings described here relate only to CS-1 imperative programming - algorithmic problems within an institution-based sample ( $N=400$ ); the expert-designed ontology and knowledge base deliberately sacrifice scalability for explainability, while generalizability necessitates institutional validation. Abstract: Mission-critical enterprise domains demand AI systems that are not merely reactive interpreters of user prompts, but proactive agents capable of planning, constrained reasoning, and reliable execution. Abstract: Learning-based software vulnerability detection has progressed rapidly; however, most of research studies focus on C/C++ and Java and emphasize detection accuracy alone. Python, despite its extensive use in security-critical and web-based systems, remains comparatively underexplored. Existing Python-focused approaches typically assess a limited range of vulnerability types and rarely examine robustness, confidence calibration, or deployment efficiency—factors essential for real-world Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) integration. This study introduces DeepSecure, a robust and deployment-ready deep learning framework for detecting security vulnerabilities in Python source code. The framework integrates a transformer encoder (CodeBERT or GraphCodeBERT) with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) pooling layers to capture complementary semantic, sequential, and localized vulnerability patterns. DeepSecure was evaluated across six vulnerability categories: SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting, Command Injection, Remote Code Execution, Broken Authentication, and Hard-coded Credentials, including two newly curated authentication-related datasets. A robustness-oriented protocol using five random seeds was adopted. Performance was measured using precision, recall, F1, and macro-F1, while reliability was assessed using Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Deployment feasibility was evaluated through inference latency and throughput. DeepSecure achieved a macro-averaged F1-score of 96.93%, outperforming prior Python-based baselines by 11.16 percentage points. GraphCodeBERT showed a non-significant trend toward lower macro-averaged ECE (0.1902 vs. 0.2540), with the advantage most pronounced for injection-type vulnerabilities. Multi-seed experiments showed performance variation below 0.5%, and deployment tests demonstrated throughput above 440 samples per second with latency below 2.3 ms, supporting real-time CI/CD integration.

Publication Title: IEEE Control Systems Letters
Abstract: Energy demands from data centers have surged and stressed the grid in recent years. Electric grids require balancing supply and demand every second, motivating demand response (reduction) from large loads, including data centers. This can be achieved by rescheduling jobs on a physical machine. Its real-time implementation is uncertain due to fluctuating resource utilization, and rescheduling incurs quality-of-service (QoS) losses that providers are unwilling to disclose. We propose a restless multi-armed bandit (RMAB) framework, in which the grid operator requests load reductions without access to detailed job-rescheduling procedures. Using open-source virtual machine (VM) datasets, we model job arrivals and rescheduling at each data center as a restless arm in a Markov decision process (MDP) and derive Whittle-index-based policies using the learned transition function via Thompson sampling. To overcome the weakness of an increasingly long learning process due to an enlarged state space, we use a mixed strategy that includes a global upper confidence bound (UCB) and encodes with trust indices to enhance robustness and accelerate learning. Results show that the proposed mixed-strategy algorithm remains robust across varying state-space sizes and consistently outperforms the pure Thompson-Whittle (TW) algorithm, especially when contextual information is noisy. It also demonstrates superior performance compared to the state-of-the-art EXP4 framework. We provided open-source code to ensure reproducibility.

Abstract: Security of voice transmission in modern wireless communication is a key issue, particularly in defense, public safety, and emergency response systems where sensitive information is shared in real time. This paper presents the implementation of a secure voice communication system utilizing both GNU Radio and the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption. The offered structure encrypts analog voice input with AES-128 and sends it over a software-defined radio (SDR) channel to ensure secure end-to-end communication. On the receiver side, the real-time encrypted data is demodulated and decrypted to restore the original audio signal. GNU Radio Companion (GRC) simulates the system with custom Python encoding blocks embedded in the SDR flowgraph. Viewed experimentally, the proposed technique ensures low-latency transmission of high-quality audio at a low bit error rate and at a low computational cost. The solution offers a scalable and flexible method of secure, inexpensive, and real-time voice communication, applicable to both tactical and civilian wireless voice communications.

Abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) requires communication technologies that combine long-range connectivity, energy efficiency, bounded latency, and seamless mobility. Conventional LoRaWAN, based on a single-hop star topology and ALOHA medium access, suffers from high collision rates and limited mobility support, resulting in missed deadlines and reduced reliability in dynamic deployments. This paper presents MAR-LoRa (Mobility-Aware LoRa Protocol for Reliable IoT Communications). This enhanced protocol integrates lightweight RSSI-variance mobility detection, proactive make-before-break handovers, and adaptive parameter control within a deterministic TDMA superframe. Specifically, MAR-LoRa enables nodes to 1) detect mobility locally with minimal overhead, 2) perform seamless handovers before link failure, and 3) dynamically adjust spreading factor and channel to maintain reliability and fairness. A Python-based discrete-event simulator was developed to evaluate performance across 35–1000 nodes under sequential and asynchronous traffic patterns. Compared with baseline MRT-LoRa, MAR-LoRa eliminates node isolation and collisions in mobile settings, improves the mean Packet Delivery Ratio by up to 21.5 percentage points relative to MRT-LoRa (averaged across 3–4 independent simulation runs per configuration), and increases Jain’s fairness index by up to 0.58, while incurring only a bounded latency overhead of 2–30 seconds per superframe. These results demonstrate that MAR-LoRa achieves scalable, mobility-resilient, and real-time performance, advancing the suitability of LoRa for next-generation IIoT applications.

Abstract: Reliable environmental monitoring requires resilience against sensor node failures to ensure continuous data acquisition. Abstract: A contemporary high performance computing systems often use a static model of concurrency where the configurations for thread pools are defined at either compile time or application initialization through heuristically derived approximations. This paper proposes a novel Adaptive Parallel Search Framework that integrates the lightweight concurrency primitives of Java 21 Virtual Threads with real-time Micro meter-based observability to establish a closed-loop autonomic control system. Abstract: Malicious Python packages make software supply chains vulnerable by exploiting trust in open-source repositories like Python Package Index (PyPI). Abstract: Institutional discourse is increasingly produced and read with AI assistance, yet no tool currently exists to evaluate its structural epistemic properties automatically and reproducibly. Second, a register-mismatch gradient: the engine achieves 6/6 gate classification on synthetic institutional texts and consistent structural bifurcation on SEC regulatory filings, but produces $\kappa=0.053$ (Gemini) and $\kappa=0.000$ (GPT) against the MAFALDA informal-argumentation corpus, empirically establishing that institutional structural constructs (evasion, authority laundering, defensive routines) do not map onto general-purpose argumentation fallacies. Third, a scale contrast with institutional annotation precedent: the European Commission's JRC campaigns required over seventy scholars annotating 2,500 documents across nine languages with months of calibration and persistent expert disagreement; the deterministic kernel produces reproducible output on 69 documents with fully documented failure modes and no inter-annotator calibration requirement.

Abstract: Energy consumption in modern buildings keeps increasing because of the inefficient operation of lighting, heating, and cooling systems that are unable to adapt to real-time occupancy and environmental variations. Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show high accuracy in solving mathematical word problems, but in reality, LLMs do not perform arithmetic computations during prediction; they only generate tokens. The evaluation of LLMs on BIG-bench expression-based benchmarks reveals the reality, where even state-of-the-art LLMs obtain near-zero accuracy in solving multistep arithmetic problems, irrespective of their scale. The issue is not fixed by fine-tuning LLMs, as it is an architectural limitation. This paper proposes an agent-based solution that fixes the limitation by strictly separating two agents: a lightweight Orchestrator Agent responsible for natural language processing and tool management, and an MCP Calculator Server providing an agentic_calculator tool accessible via internal deterministic MathJS expressions. The MathJS DSL is different from traditional Python-based code interpreters, as it is safe by design, does not require sandboxing, and is executed inline. The proposed framework, implemented using four benchmarks and two LLM backends (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Opus), achieves 9699% accuracy in multi-step arithmetic problems, where LLMs alone obtain only 0-23% accuracy, in addition to providing improvements in solving word problem benchmarks.

The 12-item Introductory Programming Self-Efficacy Scale (IPSES), specifically adapted for Java programming, was used to measure self-efficacy. title: ASSENT: Learning-Based Association Optimization for Distributed Cell-Free ISAC

Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a key emerging 6G technology. Despite progress, ISAC still lacks scalable methods for joint access point (AP) clustering and user/target scheduling in distributed deployments under fronthaul limits. Moreover, existing ISAC solutions largely rely on centralized processing and full channel state information, limiting scalability. This paper addresses joint AP clustering, user and target scheduling, and AP mode selection in distributed cell-free ISAC systems operating with constrained fronthaul capacity. We formulate the problem as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) that jointly captures interference coupling, RF chain limits, and sensing requirements, providing optimal but computationally demanding solutions. To enable real-time and scalable operation, we propose ASSENT (ASSociation and ENTity selection), a graph neural network (GNN) framework trained on MILP solutions to efficiently learn association and mode-selection policies directly from lightweight link statistics. Simulations show that ASSENT achieves near-optimal utility while accurately learning the underlying associations. Additionally, its single forward pass inference reduces decision latency compared to optimization-based methods. An open-source Python/PyTorch implementation with full datasets is provided to facilitate reproducible and extensible research in cell-free ISAC.

Abstract: Grammar-based test generation is widely used to test interpreters and compilers. The approach embeds generated inputs into a vector space and clusters them to construct a diversity map of the input domain. Abstract: Sign language recognition is essential in eliminating the communication barriers between hearing-impaired and speech-impaired persons and the hearing society. To counter these limitations, a segment-aware vision-based framework for dynamic sign language recognition using Vision Transformers is proposed in this paper. The segmented data is then passed to a Vision Transformer model with multi-head self-attention layers, which collectively attend to the spatially connected patches across the entire visual field. Vision Transformers, unlike CNN models that mostly consider local features, are able to learn long-range dependencies, making them ideal for the dynamic gesture recognition task. The integrated segment-aware and transformer-based feature learning scheme improves recognition efficiency, scalability, and system performance while enabling future real-time assistive communication and multilingual SL use cases.

Abstract: Accurate specification of the ionosphere is essential for mitigating the impacts of space weather on communication, navigation, and surveillance systems. title: HDPRO: Preventing Orphaned Bursts with Deterministic Sub-500ms Recovery in Kubernetes
Authors: A. Singh; A. Nemtur
Author Affiliations: NA; NA
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE Cloud Summit
Abstract: In High-Density Periodic Burst (HDPB) workloads, pods partition a large rule corpus and execute their shards simultaneously at fixed time boundaries—and a single pod failure silently orphans its entire partition. In production deployments spanning millions of rules across dozens of pods, rules go unprocessed, deadlines are missed, and the failure goes undetected for T+40s under standard Kubernetes NodeLease—the platform’s default failure detection mechanism. For workloads demanding recovery well within that window, NodeLease cannot respond before the next burst boundary has already fired and the orphaned partition has missed its cycle. This is the Orphaned Burst. We present HDPRO, a lightweight Go sidecar that prevents the Orphaned Burst by detecting pod failure in under 500ms, without modifying the control plane or worker applications.HDPRO (High-Density Periodic Resource Orchestrator) is a wall-clock-aligned 4-phase coordination sidecar: all pods determine their phase from the absolute wall clock second, guaranteeing cluster-wide synchronization regardless of pod start time. During Maintenance (:25–:50), all pods run garbage collection simultaneously, ensuring every pod enters the detection window with a clean heap. During Pre-warm (:50–:60), gossip accelerates cluster-wide to 100ms intervals, actively monitoring for pod failures. The Burst phase (:00–:10) is reserved exclusively for rule execution with no GC, no failure detection, no gossip overhead, so that when :00 fires, every pod executes at full capacity with zero background contention. On failure detection during Pre-warm, the consistent hash ring immediately reassigns rule ownership to the successor pod, completing ring ownership coordination before the next :00 boundary.We evaluate HDPRO across two independent experimental methodologies on a 5-node GKE cluster. HDPRO-Relative (4,601 events) demonstrates 429.5ms mean recovery (sigma: 14.82ms, p99: 456ms)—a 93x improvement over Kubernetes NodeLease. HDPRO-Synchronized (72 events, 100 trials) independently confirms 421.1ms mean (sigma: 9.75ms, p99: 460ms), with tighter variance proving wall-clock alignment improves detection consistency. Wall-clock alignment completely eliminates phase-skew artifacts (2,049 to 0, 100% reduction), confirming that sub-500ms orphaned burst prevention is a structural property of N-Strike, not an instrumentation artifact.The 421–429ms figure measures detection and ring coordination latency; full keyspace transfer cost in stateful backends depends on the storage layer and is left to future work.

Abstract: Solving real-time quadratic programming (QP) is a ubiquitous task in control engineering, such as in model predictive control and control barrier function-based QP. Abstract: We chose the Universal Serial Bus (USB) interface to connect our peripheral devices as its plug-and-play and compatibility features are widely adopted. This vulnerability has resulted in a growing number of sophisticated USB attacks, specifically those utilizing the BadUSB attack, wherein attackers modify device firmware to mimic legitimate hardware parts. One of these threats is the Human Interface Device (HID)based attacks that poses an acute and feasible threat. Evil USB devices like the USB Rubber Ducky act as keyboards injecting a sequence of commands at high speed allowing access to systems, malware plants and data exfiltration. As these inputs are considered valid user actions, traditional security measures like antivirus and access controls usually cannot identify or block them. The following work presents a detailed and structured survey regarding current methods of detection and prevention of attacks carried out using HID interfaces in particular. Based on the literature review, previous works on detection and prevention can be classified as monitoring systems for hardware level detection, behavior-based detection approaches, sandboxing isolation techniques and authentication oriented systems. Each of the aforementioned approaches will be explored in more details and its advantages and drawbacks will be discussed including issues such as effectiveness, complexity, real-time capabilities and resource requirements. In addition, through the course of analysis, it is possible to observe several shortcomings of the existing solutions which are required to use special-purpose hardware (e.g., for virtual machine creation and operation), exhibit high implementation complexity, will cause significant latency overhead and, if behavior-based systems are used, produce false positives. Furthermore, some approaches have been developed separately from one another and lack integration of multiple detection layers into one coherent system. Therefore, a possible approach to overcome all the mentioned drawbacks might include creating a hybrid detection system which combines the use of behavior analysis along with classification of devices to ensure efficient and real-time detection of malicious HID devices without any additional hardware requirements.

Abstract: The Automated Teller Machine (ATM) is a significant element of today's banking technology, however it continues to have issues associated with access and damage from non-authorized persons, vandalization, and impersonation fraud. This report will provide a comprehensive description of a Face Detection and Alert System which integrates in real-time, face recognition, mask detection and crowd surveillance and also includes an advanced alert notification system utilizing Twilio's API. When a real-time event occurs (i.e., when an unknown individual approaches the ATM, there is no visible face on the camera, etc.) the system automatically sends an SMS message with an image to the registered bank account owner. The entire system was developed using OpenCV, TensorFlow/Keras and Python to enable fast video processing and CSV to enable scalable user management. Testing of the proposed system demonstrated a greater than 70 % improvement in response time to a potential ATM threat and reduced false alarms by approximately 27 % over current detection methods. Abstract: This research aims to illustrate what actually takes place with the data that is collected from IoT devices as it flows into Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems, showing how this integration transforms the way businesses reach and engage customers. Integrating live streams – such as usage traces, performance variations, and device-level error logs – closes this latency gap by enabling immediate, context-aware business actions. Using a synthetically generated dataset of 455 smart-home user transactions, this study demonstrates how dense, high-velocity IoT data can be used to reveal behavioral patterns that remain invisible in conventional CRM environments. Although the technical pipeline is straightforward - data preprocessing using Python; the structured SQL queries, and Tableau visualizations mapping device activity to customer engagement – the data itself is rich, containing signals of genuine user behavior. Real-time data enables both informed decision-making as well as hyper-personalization. Empirical results show higher retention, lower churn and faster support resolution when CRM systems respond the moment an IoT signal is generated – whether due to malfunction, usage anomalies, or performance degradation. The objective extends beyond automation for its own sake; the focus is on optimal timing— engaging customers precisely when intervention is most valuable. The key finding demonstrates that when IoT and CRM operate synergistically, they create a feedback loop capable of generating value at increasing speed. Data velocity translates into enhanced trust, relevance, and ultimately customer loyalty. This research illustrates how customer engagement scales effectively in continuously connected environments.

Abstract: Solid-state nanopores have emerged as a versatile, label-free platform for single-molecule sensing. However, conventional ex situ fabrication techniques, such as focused ion beam milling and transmission electron microscopy drilling, are constrained by high cost, low throughput, and dependence on specialized instrumentation, limiting their widespread adoption and scalability. In situ fabrication based on controlled dielectric breakdown (CDB) greatly simplifies the process, yet existing implementations often remain expensive and rely on proprietary software, restricting flexibility for method development. Here, we present P.O.R.E., a low-cost, compact and programmable system for controlled dielectric breakdown nanopore formation. This platform achieves system-level miniaturization and cost reduction without sacrificing electrical precision. Its compact control circuit and modular hardware design enable convenient, high-fidelity interfacing with nanopore chips and peripheral components. A Python-based software interface provides real-time monitoring, programmable feedback control, and an observer-based scheme for real-time pore-size estimation, while offering extensibility for diverse fabrication protocols. The system is USB-powered and smartphone-sized, with the core electronic hardware costs less than 100 US dollars, significantly lowering the barrier to entry. Experimental validation demonstrates nanopore formation across the 6–20 nm range, with stable electrical characteristics and low-frequency noise. DNA and protein translocation measurements acquired using a dedicated low-noise amplifier further confirm the downstream sensing functionality of the fabricated pores. This work establishes an accessible and extensible platform for solid-state nanopore fabrication and provides a foundation for future expansion toward more automated and parallel fabrication workflows.

Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are computational models inspired by the event-driven communication and connectivity patterns of biological neural circuits. They enable high energy efficiency and natural support for diverse architectures ranging from layered networks to small-world and graphstructured topologies. In this work, we introduce NeuroCoreX, an open-source, FPGA-based spiking neural network emulator that provides real-time, on-chip learning and flexible network organization. NeuroCoreX supports both feedforward sensory inputs streamed directly from sensors or PCs via UART and recurrent on-chip connectivity, enabling simultaneous processing and learning from external stimuli and internal network dynamics-capabilities rarely available in existing FPGA SNN platforms. The system implements a Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron model with current-based synapses and supports pair-based STDP learning on both feedforward and recurrent synapses. A lightweight Python interface enables interactive configuration, live monitoring, weight read-back, and experiment control. Importantly, NeuroCoreX is tightly integrated with the SuperNeuroMAT simulator, allowing SNN models to be transferred seamlessly from software to hardware for hardware-in-the-loop development. By combining real-time plasticity, flexible connectivity, and an open-source VHDL implementation, NeuroCoreX provides an extensible and accessible platform for neuromorphic research, algorithm-hardware co-design, and energy-efficient edge intelligence.

These results show that procedural structure in the prompt drives execution fidelity in this controlled offline benchmark; they do not establish suitability for real-time closed-loop traffic control and instead support LLM use only within guarded decision-support pipelines with deterministic validation.

Abstract: Sky Scout is a state of the art weather software intended to give users real time weather forecasts and air quality information, with a clean desktop interface. The user interface presents this data in an easy to use and attractive design. The Sky Scout software provides unique opportunities for using a 7 day weather forecast, live Air Quality Index, and a hands free city search using voice. The design of the application was created in a responsive manner and optimized with creative and dynamic backgrounds and hover tooltips to make the program easier to use. This research section will cover the program architecture, workflow development, and data presentation for streaming data in order to visualize data that would be of interest to users in some manner; namely, live, accurate, relevant, useful, and actionable environmental information. User surveys indicated that prior to seeing and using the interface that all users were very supportive of the long term use of the Sky Scout interface, the clarity of information presented, and the ease of interaction. title: Shiro: Efficient and Accurate In-Storage Data Lifetime Separation for nand Flash SSDs
Authors: P. Sun; S. Zheng; L. You; W. Zhang; R. Ma; J. Yang; F. Zhu; S. Li; L. Huang
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China; MoE Key Laboratory of Artificial Intelligence, AI Institute, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China; School of Computer Science and Technology, Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou, China; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China; Alibaba Cloud, Hangzhou, China; Alibaba Cloud, Hangzhou, China; Alibaba Cloud, Hangzhou, China; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
Abstract: The log-structured nature of nand flash storage necessitates garbage collection (GC) in solid state drives (SSDs). GC is a major source of runtime write amplification (WA), leading to faster device wear out and interference with host I/Os. The key to mitigating this problem is separating data by lifetime so that data in the same flash block are invalidated within temporal proximity. For higher lifetime prediction accuracy and adaptibility, prior works proposed using machine learning (ML) algorithms for data separation. However, existing learning-based solutions perform data lifetime prediction at the host side, leading to several drawbacks. First, host-side prediction does not have knowledge of the internal data movement inside the SSD during GC, and thus fails to leverage the opportunity to further separate GC writes, resulting in suboptimal WA reduction in the long term. Second, performing prediction at the host significantly prolongs the I/O critical path and consumes host resources that could otherwise be used for serving user applications. We present Shiro, a holistic flash translation layer (FTL) design that performs in-storage data separation for both user writes and GC writes for maximal long-term WA reduction. For user writes, Shiro uses a sequence model to accurately predict data lifetime by learning lifetime distribution from long historical access patterns. For GC writes, Shiro incorporates a reinforcement learning-assisted page migration strategy that takes direct feedback from long-term WA to further improve data separation efficacy. To address the challenges posed by performing fine-grained and real-time ML decisions inside the resource-constrained SSD, we propose a suite of enabling techniques to keep computation and storage overhead low. Extensive evaluation of Shiro on real-world traces shows that Shiro can deliver 29%–68% lower WA compared with conventional FTL and state-of-the-art in-storage data separation schemes. Furthermore, thanks to lower data migration overhead during GC, Shiro achieves significantly higher steady-state I/O performance.

title: Stress Detection and Suggestion for IT Professional Using Natural Language Processsing

Abstract: Stress has become a critical occupational hazard for IT professionals, who routinely face stringent deadlines, rapid task switching, and heavy cognitive workloads. To address these limitations, this work proposes a multimodal, automated stress-detection system that integrates image processing, physiological pattern analysis, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to enable continuous and objective monitoring of employee stress levels. Facial expression cues are extracted using Python libraries such as MediaPipe and OpenCV, which identify 33 facial landmark points as indicators of emotional strain. Textual inputs—such as user- provided statements or reflections—are processed through NLP models to identify stress-related sentiment and linguistic markers. These multimodal inputs are analysed using machine learning models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image analysis, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs/LSTMs) for physiological trends, and transformer-based NLP models for textual interpretation. The fused outputs generate a unified real-time stress score, enabling early detection and intervention. title: Investigating Stealer Malware Through Memory Forensic Analysis
Authors: S. Purbaya; R. Harwahyu
Author Affiliations: Departement of Electrical Engineering, Universitas Indonesia, Depok, Indonesia; Departement of Electrical Engineering, Universitas Indonesia, Depok, Indonesia
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Signals and Systems (ICSigSys)
Abstract: This study addresses the growing threat of credential-stealing malware that targets browser-stored credentials. It aims to identify in-memory artifacts generated during malware execution, particularly those related to unauthorized access to browser credential storage. A memory forensics approach was implemented using a custom Python script to monitor real-time access to Chrome’s Login Data file via Sysinternals’ handle.exe. Multiple stealer malware samples—Lumma, RedLine, Vidar, and Gremlin—were executed in a controlled sandbox environment. Memory was acquired at the moment of credential access and analyzed using Volatility3 to extract artifacts and identify behavioral patterns. The results reveal consistent in-memory behaviors across the analyzed stealer samples, including unauthorized access to credential storage and the use of chrome.exe through process injection or spawning. These findings indicate a shared operational strategy among stealer malware. The study demonstrates that memory forensics is effective for uncovering runtime artifacts that are not observable through disk-based analysis. However, the approach depends on precise acquisition timing and controlled environments, which may affect completeness and generalizability. Despite these limitations, this work provides an event-driven forensic methodology that supports more accurate artifact-based detection and future development of real-time memory analysis techniques.

Abstract: This article analyses the performance characteristics of XGBoost models across multiple datasets for phishing URL detection, extending our previous conference paper with comprehensive cross-dataset validation and comparative analysis. Our approach addresses the issue of feature instability, showing how balanced feature engineering is crucial for reliable detection. The model achieves 90.7% accuracy and 91.2% F1 score on the custom dataset, with a solid 77.8% average accuracy across three independent test sets. Although Neural Networks offered faster inference (7.51ms vs 20.6ms) and smaller model sizes, XGBoost’s balance of high accuracy and rapid training makes it highly effective for practical, real-world phishing detection systems.

title: Low-Code and No-Code Platforms for Linux System Administration: A SWOT Analysis
Authors: J. W. Horsky; A. M. Saghiri

Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computer, Data Sciences and Applications (ACDSA)
Abstract: We present a structured SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis of low-code and no-code (LCNC) platforms for Linux system administration. We compare n8n, Zapier, and Make.com as representative LCNC platforms and focus on n8n because it can be self-hosted and is easily extensible. Using hands-on experiments and case studies in monitoring and service management, we compare the benefits of LCNC workflows with traditional mechanisms that rely on Bash scripting, cron and systemd timers, Python programs, and Ansible- based configuration management. Our study is guided by explicit research questions on task fit, integrability, observability, security, cost, and architecture. We complement the qualitative SWOT analysis with a simple cost-benefit discussion and lightweight performance measurements (CPU usage and end-toend latency) for representative workflows. We also comment on how LCNC platforms can orchestrate AI/ML and MLOps-style tasks in Linux environments. Our findings show that LCNC accelerates integration, centralizes credentials, and improves visibility through execution histories and traceable runs, while code-centric approaches remain stronger for tight control loops, deep service tuning, and deterministic convergence. The evidence favors hybrid architectures in which LCNC orchestrates triggers, routing, AI/ML calls, and approvals, while native Linux tools execute performance-sensitive operations. To our knowledge, this is the first study to provide a dedicated, Linux-focused SWOT analysis of LCNC platforms grounded in concrete administration tasks.

Abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensors are commonly utilized for refractive index-based sensing owing to their real-time detection capabilities and elevated sensitivity. First, the standard Kretschmann setup, which consists of a prism, gold and water is simulated to check the accuracy of the proposed model. This shows a clear resonance dip and a steady angular shift as the refractive index changes. The sensitivity, Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) and overall Figure of Merit (FOM) are analysed. After that, the validated framework is used to look into dielectric-assisted, 2D material-assisted and hybrid configurations. The results show that combining 2D materials with high-index 3D dielectric layers works well to get around the problems with single-material-assisted designs by improving both sensitivity and resonance sharpness at the same time. Abstract: Incorporating learning-based models, such as artificial neural networks or Gaussian processes, into model predictive control (MPC) strategies can significantly improve control performance and online adaptation capabilities for real-world applications. title: SpecPool: Storage-Layer Speculation for Parallel Smart Contract Execution
Authors: F. Rola; M. Matos; M. Nazarewicz; P. Romano
Author Affiliations: INESC-ID, Instituto Superior Técnico, University of Lisbon, Portugal; INESC-ID, Instituto Superior Técnico, University of Lisbon, Portugal; No affiliation; INESC-ID, Instituto Superior Técnico, University of Lisbon, Portugal
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 46th International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems (ICDCS)
Abstract: Modern blockchains face execution bottlenecks as rising transaction loads exceed the limits of sequential processing, threatening scalability. Exploiting parallelism safely, while preserving determinism, is essential to address this challenge. SpecPool transforms the blockchain mempool-traditionally a passive queue-into an active preprocessing engine. While transactions await consensus, SpecPool predicts a likely block execution order using mempool-visible signals such as fees, arrival time, and coarse batching windows while respecting persender nonce ordering. It then predicts potential conflicts between transactions by combining static analysis of contract bytecode with historical access patterns. Transactions are subsequently speculatively pre-executed in parallel according to the predicted order within sandboxed environments, extracting transaction read/write sets and invocation chains. This metadata enables conflict-aware validation, maximizing concurrency while preserving consensus-consistent ordering. Operating at the storage layer, SpecPool requires no modifications to virtual machine semantics or consensus protocols, simplifying adoption in existing blockchain systems. We implement SpecPool in the Cosmos framework and evaluate it using workloads derived from the Injective blockchain. Experiments demonstrate up to a $60 \times$ reduction in block validation latency and 20% throughput improvement over prior parallel execution approaches. We additionally analyze the effects of block predictability and transaction mempool visibility in a high-frequency blockchain, showing that SpecPool maintains accurate order prediction and effective parallelism even under Injective's block time of 0.63 seconds.
Author Keywords: mempool optimization;blockchain systems;parallel transaction validation;conflict-aware scheduling

Abstract: To address the challenges of autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance for Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) in dynamic and uncertain environments, this paper proposes a robust hybrid framework integrating the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm, and the Velocity Obstacle (VO) method. The EKF module is employed to mitigate sensor noise, providing accurate state estimations for the system. TD3 serves as the core policy optimizer, enabling the learning of autonomous obstacle avoidance strategies within a continuous action space. A key innovation of this study is the introduction of the VO module as a dual-purpose safety mechanism. During training, constraint shaping is utilized to project and correct the action space, providing explicit guidance for the neural network's policy search. This significantly reduces unguided exploration and accelerates convergence. During execution, the VO module acts as a real-time safety shield, projecting potentially unsafe actions into a feasible control set to ensure immediate collision avoidance for USVs under critical conditions. The performance of the proposed framework was validated in a high-fidelity Python-based simulation environment. Experimental results demonstrate that in complex scenarios featuring both observation noise and dynamic obstacles, the EKF-TD3-VO framework significantly outperforms the baseline TD3 method in terms of obstacle avoidance success rate and trajectory smoothness. Attributed to the structural guidance and safety shielding of the VO module, the system's training efficiency and decision-making robustness are substantially enhanced. This study establishes a practical technical foundation for risk-aware navigation and safe decision-making in autonomous marine robotic systems.

Abstract: There is an increase in complexity in the power system due to integration with renewables and dynamic modelling of the system. It is essential to maintain the transient stability of the system along with its safe, reliable and secure operation. In the present manuscript, for the analysis of power systems' stability, ML and data-driven approaches are investigated in detail as these approaches exhibit high accuracy, real-time applicability and the ability to model non-linear dynamics. The transient stability of the New England 39-Bus Test System dataset has been classified as ‘stable’ or ‘unstable’ using five different ML algorithms, which are the Random Forest (RFA), the Logistic Regression (LR), the Artificial Neural Network (ANN), the Support Vector Machine (SVM) and the Decision Tree (DT). The features of the dataset are derived using a Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU). The best results are obtained with RFA, which showed an accuracy of 0.99, recall =1.00, precision=0.99, and F1-score of 1.00. The RFA showed an area under the curve value of 1.00 and outperformed the other classifiers/algorithms. The work is further extended with the SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) framework from Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for interpreting the RFA predictions. The results from the fusion of RFA and SHAP showed IqG7, VAIvB27 and IqG9 as the most influential features that govern the system's stability. Different SHAP plots, like the waterfall plot, bee swarm plot and decision plots, are shown to explain the contributions by features of the dataset in enhancing the transparency and interpretability of the model. This work bridges the theoretical advancements in ML and SHAP/XAI with transient stability assessment and the reliability of the power system. The unique contribution of this work is the fusion of RFA and XAI, which provides an opportunity for improving the power systems' efficiency, reliability, stability, interpretability and transparency of the system. It contributes to meeting goal 7 of 17 Sustainable Development Goals SDGs This work, developed in Python with a Google Colab environment, paves the path for a secure, faster, smarter and more resilient grid operations.

Abstract: Cloud computing serves as the primary infrastructure for scalable Artificial Intelligence (AI) workloads, yet selecting the optimal deployment paradigm remains a critical challenge for practitioners. This research presents a structured empirical comparison between Function-as-a-Service (Serverless) and Virtual Machine (VM)-based models using a “single-image, dual-deployment” benchmarking framework on Microsoft Azure. We evaluate these architectures across diverse AI tasks, including MobileNetV2 image classification, Librosa audio feature extraction, and NLP training. Abstract: Numerical optimization (solving optimization problems using digital computers) currently dominates but has three drawbacks: high energy consumption, poor scalability, and lack of an execution time certificate. This equation certifies that the settling time (execution time) is independent of the dimension of the optimization problems and can be arbitrarily small if the analog computer allows.

Author Affiliations: Faculty of Computer Sciences, MSA University, Giza, Egypt; Faculty of Computer Sciences, MSA University, Giza, Egypt; Faculty of Computer Sciences, MSA University, Giza, Egypt; Faculty of Computer Sciences, MSA University, Giza, Egypt
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Systems, and Emerging Technologies (ICAISET)
Abstract: Sign language is considered the main linguistic bridge for the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing community; however, a continuous communication gap still exists because only a limited number of hearing individuals have achieved fluency in sign languages. This study presents an efficient vision-based deep learning system for recognizing Egyptian Sign Language (ESL) using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning techniques.The proposed models were developed using a dataset that contains 20 signs that are frequently used in everyday life in Egypt, expressed in two different forms according to the Egyptian dialect and Standard Arabic.The Model’s accuracy was evaluated through the integration of spatial feature extraction using CNNs with temporal modeling to capture sign motion, specifically employing the VGG16 architecture. To measure real-world hand and body landmarks, Media Pipe Holistic was utilized to enhance recognition performance during testing. The experimental results indicate that the VGG16-based model achieved an overall accuracy of 96.12%, while the CNN-based model achieved an overall accuracy of 96%. To further develop and validate the proposed algorithm, a real-time graphical user interface application was created for sign prediction. These results establish the proposed framework as a scalable and effective solution for automating sign language recognition and improving the overall quality of life for individuals in the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing communities.In this paper, Arabic Sign Language is referred to as ArSL to avoid confusion with American Sign Language (ASL).

title: A Comprehensive and Systematic Review of Wearable and Vision-based Sign Language Translation Systems
Authors: A. R; A. Vinod; A. R. N; J. P. R
Author Affiliations: Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Amritapuri, India; Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Amritapuri, India; Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Amritapuri, India; Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Amritapuri, India
Publication Title: 2026 9th International Conference on Computing Methodologies and Communication (ICCMC)
Abstract: Over 466 million people worldwide experience disabling hearing loss, projected to reach 900 million by 2050. Indian Sign Language (ISL) serves approximately 5 million deaf individuals in India, yet no large-scale public ISL dataset exists a critical research gap. This paper addresses three core objectives: (i) systematically compare wearable and vision-based sensing modalities; (ii) evaluate temporal modelling techniques from rule-based ML to Transformer-based large vision models; and (iii) identify actionable research directions for low-resource ISL systems. Through structured analysis of peer-reviewed publications, we survey comparative datasets (WLASL, Multi-VSL, KArSL), embedded deployment constraints, and real-time performance trade-offs. Key findings: Bi-GRU achieves 98.93% accuracy vs. 97.87% for Bi-LSTM with lower computational cost; SignVLM delivers state-of-the-art zero-shot generalization on large-vocabulary comparatives; and the absence of a standardized public ISL dataset remains the most critical open gap. Ten structured open challenges with actionable research directions are identified.

title: AI-Powered Sign Language Translator
Authors: B. Ray; A. Al Rifat; A. Sattar
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science & Engineering, Daffodil International University, Dhaka, Bangladesh; Department of Computer Science & Engineering, Daffodil International University, Dhaka, Bangladesh; Department of Computer Science & Engineering, Daffodil International University, Dhaka, Bangladesh

Abstract: In this paper, I describe a Bangla Sign Language (BdSL) translator, which identifies 60 dynamic signs with the help of landmark-based machine learning methods. The purpose of the system is to eliminate the communications barrier between the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing population and the hearing population in Bangladesh by translating the sign language to text. A multi-stage preprocessing pipeline is trained which includes MediaPipe Holistic landmark extraction, coordinate normalization and temporal quantization which convert the gesture videos into a format of structured sequential feature representations. Four methods of classification are considered, and they are LSTM-based temporal models and conventional machine learning models. The experimental findings have indicated that temporal modeling has a great contribution to recognition performance. The LSTM-D5MAX set has the best performance with the highest accuracy and good discriminative properties of 76.90 percent, and the performances of DTW-SVM and regular LSTM are moderate. In its turn, the classical SVM demonstrates low efficiency as it is incapable of capturing temporal dependencies. The proposed system guarantees the privacy of users since it does not make use of raw video frames but only skeletal landmark data which is computationally efficient enough to be used in real-time mode. This work provides a scalable base to more vocabulary BdSL translation systems and leads to privacy-protective intelligent assistive communication technologies.

Abstract: The barriers to communication between hearing and speech impaired people and the general populace still exist because of the lack of knowledge with regards to the sign language. In this paper, I am going to introduce an Emotion-Aware Multilingual Sign Language Interpretation System based on Deep Learning which allows interpreting signs in real-time with both emotional and contextual meaning behind it. The presented system tracks hand movements and facial expressions with the help of a regular camera, recognizes gestures with the help of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and interprets continuous stream of gestures with the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. It also has facial emotion recognition, which is used to determine the emotional status of the user (happy, sad, fear, neutral), and multilingual translation, which is used to generate English-to-Tamil. Abstract: Fingerspelling is very important part of sign language communication which is a vital mode of communication for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) community. However, the problem is that the communication in form of sign language is not easily understood by ordinary people. Consequently, it poses serious challenges to deaf people in conveying their messages to those people who are unfamiliar with sign language. To address this issue, this paper introduces a multi-angle comprehensive data set of continuous finger spelling of Pakistan Sign Language (PSL) as well as proposes a spatiotemporal segmentation based framework by employing state-of-the-art models and tools such as MediaPipe, YOLO, ResNet and VGG along with segmentation and post-processing algorithms. title: Beyond Words: An Intelligent British Sign Language Dataset for AI-Driven Assistive Communication Systems
Authors: B. R. Sricharan; B. Venkatramana; P. Madduru; L. Shravani
Author Affiliations: Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning, Prasanthi Nilayam, India; Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning, Prasanthi Nilayam, India; Founder & CEO Silence Speaks, England, United Kingdom; Bhamidipati AI Data Engineer Intern Silence Speaks, England, United Kingdom

Abstract: British Sign Language is a vital communication tool for over 87,000 individuals in the UK. Yet, the lack of large-scale, standardized datasets has hindered advancements in sign language recognition and translation. This paper presents a comprehensive dataset of over 35,000 high-quality BSL videos, systematically sourced and structured for machine learning and natural language processing applications. Details the data collection, organization, and preprocessing methodologies while addressing key challenges such as data imbalance, video variability, and standardization issues. By leveraging automated processing, metadata enrichment, and generative AI-based synthesis, the work enhances sign language accessibility. It enables real-time recognition, translation, and AI-driven communication tools. This dataset serves as a foundation for next-generation sign language technologies, driving inclusivity and breaking communication barriers for the deaf community. The experimental investigation evaluates the performance of AI-based sign language recognition using a large dataset comprising 35,486 videos and 31,949 words of BSL. Alphabetwise analysis demonstrates good coverage of letters, with a high number of videos containing S(4,053), C(3,552), and P (2,737), indicating rich lexical coverage. Still, slim classes such as X (16 videos; 15 words), Z (54 videos; 50 words), and Q (127 videos; 113 words) indicate a high degree of imbalance. Interdataset variability is verified by heatmap and distribution analysis of BSL SignBank (5785), SignBSL (17035), and SpreadTheSign (1266). These results highlight the importance of balanced sampling and sample normalization in developing robust and objective sign language recognition and assistive communication systems.

title: A Vision-Based System for Automated Sign Language Teaching
Authors: K. Blekos; D. Kosmopoulos; K. Antzakas
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Engineering and Informatics, University of Patras, Patras, Greece; Department of Computer Engineering and Informatics, University of Patras, Patras, Greece; Department of Educational Sciences and Social Work, University of Patras, Patras, Greece
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies
Abstract: Sign languages are used by millions of individuals who are deaf or hard-of-hearing worldwide, yet learning them can be challenging due to limited access to qualified instructors and real-time feedback. Sign language learning is crucial for inclusion and accessible communication; however, existing e-learning solutions often fail to provide detailed or explainable feedback. To address this gap, we present a novel computer-assisted system that leverages computer vision and machine learning to teach sign languages. In our approach, students follow prerecorded videos of an instructor performing signs, and the system captures the students’ own sign production through a conventional webcam. By analyzing both static handshapes and dynamic trajectories, our method provides detailed and explainable feedback at the level of keyframes, pointing out specific misalignments in hand, wrist, and motion path. This differs from many existing tools that offer only binary correct/incorrect evaluations without guidance for improvement. We implemented the system as a prototype with a full curriculum and conducted a pilot usability evaluation with 43 participants, ranging from beginners to skilled signers. Results indicate that users found the platform intuitive, the feedback mechanism informative, and the overall experience motivating for continued practice. The pilot assessed user perceptions of usability and feedback quality; learning outcomes were not measured in this initial evaluation. Notably, our design is language-agnostic, enabling broad application across different sign language communities. By offering instant fine-grained feedback, our system aims to improve self-guided learning of sign languages and promote greater accessibility, ultimately bridging communication gaps and fostering inclusion for the Deaf community.

title: CTAG: Context-Aware Trust Graph Algebra for Multi-Level Trust Evaluation in Heterogeneous On-Chain Social Networks
Authors: Z. Ma; E. Cai; W. Xing; M. Yan; L. Liu; M. Han; Y. Chen
Author Affiliations: Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China; Binjiang Institute of Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China; Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China; University of North Georgia, United States; Saint Joseph’s University, United States; Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China; Zhejiang Shuren University, Hangzhou, China
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Software Services Engineering (SSE)
Abstract: As blockchain technology extends into societal-scale applications, dynamic service interactions (e.g., e-commerce, e-government, and social computing) are becoming increasingly complex. This renders traditional single-dimensional trust metrics insufficient for the security demands of heterogeneous Web3 service ecosystems. This paper presents a multi-level node trust evaluation framework named Context-Aware Trust Graph Algebra (CTAG). Based on algebraic graph theory, the framework defines a formal trust graph model and characterizes dynamic interaction environments precisely through the introduction of a "Scene Sextuplet." The core contribution of CTAG lies in overcoming the limitations of traditional context-agnostic models, seamlessly supporting diverse on-chain service interaction scenarios, including C2C, B2C, B2B, G2B, and G2C. By employing three distinct operators—Trust Decay, Propagation, and Composition—CTAG addresses the issue of semantic loss during cross-scene trust transmission. Furthermore, to address the challenge of trust security level classification, the model integrates Privacy Level and Governance Rule parameters. This enables fine-grained authorization management, ensuring the dynamic adjustment of trust policies across contexts with varying security requirements. We implemented a high-performance system component (TrustEngine) in Python, which encapsulates graph operation interfaces for context-aware trust evaluation. Experimental results on controlled deterministic scenarios show that CTAG exhibits context-sensitive behaviors, including cross-scene attenuation, multi-hop propagation, multi-path composition, and stable scene extension, while maintaining low query latency compared with a topology-based PageRank baseline in the tested setting. Dynamic scene extension tests further indicate that CTAG can preserve existing scene-specific trust values when new service contexts are introduced. This study provides an interpretable algebraic basis and core algorithmic components for scalable distributed identity authentication and service trust management systems.

title: MedFusion: A Unified AI Framework for Patient Interaction and Clinical Intelligence
Authors: R. H. Kumar; S. R; V. P. B; H. Yadav; S. Krishnan
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Amrita School of Computing, Bengaluru Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Amrita School of Computing, Bengaluru Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Amrita School of Computing, Bengaluru Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Amrita School of Computing, Bengaluru Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Amrita School of Computing, Bengaluru Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, India

Abstract: At present, healthcare professionals experience inefficiency due to the disconnect between clinical documentation and diagnostic imaging analyses. “MedFusion” is an innovative AI-based platform that combines diagnostic imaging with verbal patient/physician interactions using a single source of capture. The MedFusion platform employs a sequential multi-modal pipeline. The conversation captures audio from patient interviewes through the use of OpenAI's WHISPER, then processes the data through the MTS-Dialog Dataset to extract factual content. In parallel, the image analysis captures images with a Vision Transformer Encoder and a DistilGPT2 Decoder. Objective radiologic findings for the patient are extracted from the images and enhanced with knowledge gained from the Radiology Objects in Context (ROCO) dataset. The major difference between MedFusion and current multimodal healthcare AI frameworks using end-to-end generation or loosely coupled pipelines is that MedFusion proposes a deterministic fusion engine, which guarantees the clinical safety by producing no hallucinations during the integration of structured medical images and unstructured conversation data. MedFusion characterizes the capture and extracts/constructs the reports based on the software systems used to analyze and process the images. Experimental results revealed that, measured using the ROUGE-L score, the ViT-GPT2 architecture obtained a score of 0.3, and that the training loss for the architecture converged to below 0.1 over 20 epochs. Additionally, the report assembly (fusing) by the MedFusion Engine occurred in less than 0.01 seconds. MedFusion combines capabilities that allow a tool to simultaneously “see” and “hear” from the same patient data, rather than creating new information, and uses the software developed using PyTorch and Python to drive the MedFusion platform to help alleviate the administrative burden placed on healthcare practitioners and increase diagnostic accuracy.

title: Architecture-Aware Neural Compression for TriCore Firmware Using Knowledge Distillation
Authors: H. Lee; H. Kim; D. Park
Author Affiliations: School of Electronic and Electrical Engineering, Kyungpook National University, Daegu, Republic of Korea; School of Electronic and Electrical Engineering, Kyungpook National University, Daegu, Republic of Korea; School of Electronic and Electrical Engineering, Kyungpook National University, Daegu, Republic of Korea
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Information and Communication (ICAIIC)
Abstract: The transition toward Software-Defined Vehicles (SDVs) has significantly increased the complexity and size of automotive ECU firmware, posing growing challenges in hardware cost (BOM) and over-the-air (OTA) update efficiency. Conventional general-purpose compressors fail to exploit the architectural characteristics of the TriCore processor, resulting in limited compression efficiency. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an AI-driven, architecture-aware compression framework tailored for TriCore-based firmware. The proposed method employs a two-stage knowledge distillation scheme, in which a large Transformer-based Teacher model transfers its learned representations of TriCore binary patterns to a lightweight GRU-based Student model suitable for on-device deployment in real ECUs. Experimental results show that the Student-based compression framework achieves an average compression efficiency of 1.524 bpb, corresponding to 19.05% of the original firmware size on the TC375 dataset, which represents an improvement of approximately 38% compared to conventional general-purpose compressors. In addition, the proposed approach exhibits a compact runtime memory footprint during decompression, requiring only 0.25 MB, which is approximately 94% lower than that of traditional methods. Furthermore, crossvalidation between the Python reference implementation and the C-based decoder confirms deterministic and consistent decoding behavior, demonstrating the practicality and portability of the proposed framework. Overall, this study establishes a strong proof of concept for AI-driven, architecture-aware firmware compression and highlights its potential for further optimization and deployment on embedded hardware.

Author Affiliations: Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark; Academy of Wellness and Human Development, Hong Kong Baptist University Hong Kong, Hong Kong; Department of Accounting, Jiangnan University, Wuxi, China; Department of Computer Applications, Sikkim University, Sikkim, India; Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering, University of Oulu, Oulu, Finland; Department of Computing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University Hong Kong, Hong Kong

Abstract: Disease outbreaks and quarantine enforcement demand contact-free logistics solutions that eliminate human exposure while maintaining reliable supply delivery. This paper presents LLMQDelivery, an LLM-driven autonomous quadcopter logistics framework designed to minimize human contact during quarantine or biohazard situations through fully automated, language-guided delivery and retrieval of essential supplies. The system combines persistent spatial awareness, physicsaccurate manipulation, and natural language reasoning within a unified control architecture implemented in CoppeliaSim via a Python-based controller. A Large Language Model (LLM) serves as the cognitive interface, interpreting free-form instructions such as “Deliver a red medical kit to zone two” into executable multistage flight plans, eliminating the need for operators to physically interact with contaminated environments. Experimental validation involving eighteen supply objects achieved a 100% delivery success rate with centimeter-level placement accuracy and 98.5% natural language command success across 67 diverse prompts. The results demonstrate that fusion of deterministic motion control and stochastic language reasoning enables practical, cognitively autonomous UAV systems-representing a new paradigm for safe, scalable, and AI-augmented quarantine logistics.

Abstract: Insider data leakage remains a significant cybersecurity problem which existing firewalls have difficulty detecting. The paper presents an integrated firewall system which simulates quantum entanglement email verification along with end-point activity monitoring and WhatsApp-based approval. The email verification process utilizes Qiskit's simulated two-qubit states to produce deterministic quantum entangled amplitude values for basis states through hashed RY rotation angles which stop mismatches from passing through. The system employs Python tools to track USB insertion activities, capture screens and monitor clipboard functionality along with cloud accessibility. A Tkinter interface delivers warning notifications and Firebase provides secure storage for user credentials. Higher-level authorities must approve every login attempt through WhatsApp to maintain human intervention in the process. The system integrates multiple defence layers that provide scalable, proactive protection against insider threats across all industrial sectors, including those related to environmental operations.

Abstract: The issue of implementing AI agents on cloud servers is causing more issues, which the majority of people do not discuss openly. The latency is excessive, the dependability is not high enough, and in any respect of safety use it is practically unserviceable at all. Our paper is on the Agentic Edge OS-an operating system which we created ourselves based on a blank embedded board such as the Raspberry Pi 4B, to execute AI agents directly on its embedded edge hardware. To create a system that does all its thinking without the help of a cloud server, we simply created a simple Buildroot-based Linux image and coordination protocols of the Multi-Agent System. The system is based on systemd controlled Python runtime, Redis shared state and direct access to hardware via Python GPIO and PWM. Another thing that not many people have tried previously is letting agents read plain English instructions and figure out hardware wiring and GPIO mappings automatically. On our test, the edge approach is about 160 times faster than cloud configurations, as well as $1.79 \times$ faster than kernel scheduling. These figures indicate clearly that edge running intelligence is highly sensible to the robotics, industrial control, and smarter infrastructure systems.

Abstract: In this work, a demonstration of Universal Asynchronous Receiver Transmitter (UART) serial communication between the PMOD ESP32 Wi-Fi module and FPGA development boards is explored. The PMOD ESP32 Wi-Fi module has an ESP-WROOM-32 microcontroller in it, which is an integrated BT + WiFi SoC. The main objective is to establish serial communication between the Basys 3 and PYNQ Z1 boards and the PMOD ESP32 Wi-Fi module, enabling wireless connectivity through the WiFi network. UART transmitter and receiver modules are written, synthesized, and implemented on the Basys 3 using Xilinx Vivado, responsible for framing data, checking parity, and synchronizing baud rates. Real-time communication is validated through simulation waveforms and serial terminals including Putty and TeraTerm, and this process is extended to the PYNQ Z1 board. The UART module on PYNQ Z1 is designed using Vivado Block Design with AXI UartLite IP and Zynq Processor IP, and the generated bitstream is used by Python scripts in the internal Jupyter notebook to establish UART communication. The ESP-IDF framework is used to configure the PMOD ESP32 Wi-Fi module for serial communication and wireless broadcasting. These approaches provide insights on HDL-based UART design and Python-based control, demonstrating both traditional RTL FPGA design with Basys 3 and SoC-based FPGA platforms like PYNQ Z1, and can be scaled to IoT applications like home automation and Embedded Systems.

Abstract: This document describes an innovative approach to use gesture recognition to control smart home systems using computer programming (Python) along with camera (OpenCV) and multiple machine learning techniques. The system will use a combination of Random Forest, a tree based statistical model and CNNs, a type of neural network, to give an accurate result in different lighting and background environments. Abstract: Control systems operating in the real world face countless sources of unpredictable uncertainties. These random disturbances can render deterministic guarantees inapplicable and cause catastrophic safety failures. To do this we modify the traditional notion of a control barrier function (CBF) to explicitly account for these stochastic uncertainties and call these new modified functions probabilistic CBFs. Finally, we showcase the applicability of our results in simulation and hardware for the control of a quadruped robot.

Abstract: Ray tracing (RT) is a 3D graphics technique that offers highly realistic visuals. It is becoming prominent and accessible as GPU vendors have integrated dedicated ray tracing acceleration hardware. However, tracing millions of rays through 3D scenes consisting of high numbers of triangles in real time is challenging and requires expensive hardware. The main bottleneck in RT workloads is the expensive Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal task, which is a large tree structure that encodes the 3D scene. BVH traversal is a memory-bound problem, as the GPU threads spend most of their time reading tree node data from memory. In this work, we attack the memory latency bottleneck of ray tracing through prefetching. We propose a novel hardware prefetcher, named Tree Traversal Prefetcher (TTP), for ray tracing. The main idea is to leverage the existing tree traversal stack in the RT units for highly accurate prefetching. In particular, TTP prefetches nodes using the addresses already available on the hardware traversal stacks of each thread. For DFS (Depth-first search) based traversal, prefetches are generated when nodes are being popped consecutively from the traversal stack, potentially corresponding to upward traversal through the tree. We evaluate TTP on a cycle-level simulator, Vulkan-sim 2.0, and show that it achieves 1.48x speedup on average (up to 1.89x) compared to the baseline, with nearly negligible hardware overhead. TTP achieves 98.92% average L1 accuracy, which is the ratio of the prefetched blocks being actually referenced by demand loads.
