Author Affiliations: Dept of CSE, ISL Engineering Collge, Hyderabad, India; Dept of CSE, Maulana Azad National Urdu University, Hyderabad, India; Dept of CSE, Maulana Azad National Urdu University, Hyderabad, India; Department of CSE(AI&ML), Sphoorthy Engineering College Nadergul, Hyderabad; Department of CSE(AI&ML), Sphoorthy Engineering College Nadergul, Hyderabad; CSM Department, Lords Institute of Engineering and Technology, Hyderabad

Abstract: The proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the Industrial IoT (IIoT) has resulted in an unprecedented spate of data generation at network edge. But traditional cloud computing models, which were centralised and background based, struggle to meet the strict latency requirements of modern IOT ecosystems. In recent research scheme joined edge nodes and cloud servers in order to replace hybrid edge-cloud paradigms, at little cost of flexibility and QoS, but trading off experimental results which rely heavily on experiment details. New and old challenges persist in dynamically allocating resources while minimizing energy consumption and maintaining Quality of Service (QoS). This paper proposes an energy-aware hybrid edge-cloud resource optimization framework that integrates Virtual Machine (VM), container, and serverless tiers to achieve adaptive workload distribution across heterogeneous environments. The model employs Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict incoming workload patterns and Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) to regulate power utilization in real time. A multi-objective optimization function is formulated to jointly minimize energy usage, latency, and Service Level Agreement (SLA) violations while maximizing throughput and trust index.

Abstract: Ransomware presents an ever-changing threat, making use of obfuscation and polymorphism to evade traditional defense measures. This paper proposes a real-time Ransomware Detection and Intelligence Framework based on static-dynamic ML classification, a virtualized approach to behavioral monitoring, explainability, and automated reverse engineering. When samples are uploaded, they are first classified using LightGBM and LSTM models; then, the framework runs two sandbox executions in a QEMU/KVM virtual machine. In the first profiling run, the complete behavioral telemetry is collected and saved in a cloud-based service, indexed for the sample based on SHA256. In the second administrative run, featuring choreographic execution, an LLM such as GPT-5.1 suggests snapshot candidates. After the analyst approves those triggers, QMP snapshots are rapidly captured for roll-back and forensic replay, where the user can click on a process node to roll back to that particular checkpoint. Cloud-based reporting translates into visualized reports as process graphs, and open-source, GhidraMCP-based analysis leverages GPT-5.1 to support automated decompilation, pattern extraction and comprehensive reverse engineering tasks. Overall, the framework operates at a 96.8% accuracy rate, a 2.8% false-positive rate, and 1.2 seconds of inference latency, while supporting transparent detection, administrative forensic replay, and AI-assisted interaction.

title: SIA: Symbolic Interpretability for Anticipatory Deep Reinforcement Learning in Network Control
Authors: M. Jabbari; A. Duttagupta; C. Fiandrino; L. Bonati; S. D’Oro; M. Polese; M. Fiore; T. Melodia
Author Affiliations: IMDEA Networks Institute, Spain; IMDEA Networks Institute, Spain; IMDEA Networks Institute, Spain; Northeastern University, Boston, USA; Northeastern University, Boston, USA; Northeastern University, Boston, USA; IMDEA Networks Institute, Spain; Northeastern University, Boston, USA
Publication Title: IEEE INFOCOM 2026 - IEEE Conference on Computer Communications
Abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) promises adaptive control for future mobile networks but conventional agents remain reactive: they act on past and current measurements and cannot leverage short-term forecasts of exogenous Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) such as bandwidth. Augmenting agents with predictions can overcome this temporal myopia, yet uptake in networking is scarce because forecast-aware agents act as closed-boxes; operators cannot tell whether predictions guide decisions or justify the added complexity. We propose SIA, the first interpreter that exposes in real time how forecast-augmented DRL agents operate. SIA fuses Symbolic AI abstractions with per-KPI Knowledge Graphs to produce explanations, and includes a new Influence Score (IS) metric. SIA achieves sub-millisecond speed, over 200× faster than existing EXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods. We evaluate SIA on three diverse networking use cases, uncovering hidden issues, including temporal misalignment in forecast integration and reward-design biases that trigger counter-productive policies. These insights enable targeted fixes: a redesigned agent achieves a 9% higher average bitrate in video streaming, and SIA’s online Action-Refinement module improves RAN-slicing reward by 25% without retraining. By making anticipatory DRL transparent and tunable, SIA lowers the barrier to proactive control in next-generation mobile networks.

Abstract: This paper presents the design, installation, and control of a six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic manipulator based on the Product of Exponentials (POE) formulation for industrial automation tasks. The proposed system targets two representative applications, including pick-and-place object manipulation and laser-based positioning for spot-processing simulation. Forward kinematics is modeled using the POE approach, enabling a compact and singularity-consistent representation of the end-effector pose. Inverse kinematics is solved analytically by employing Paden-Kahan subproblems (Types 1, 2, and 4), which decompose the nonlinear kinematic problem into geometric substructures for efficient computation. A real-time control framework is developed in Python, integrating a graphical user interface and serial communication for intuitive interaction, trajectory input, and task execution. The hardware architecture combines a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller for coordinated actuation of six stepper motors and an Arduino Uno for end-effector control, including gripper and laser modules. Experimental validation is conducted through end-effector displacement measurement and task-space accuracy assessment, including object placement error and laser targeting deviation. Results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves reliable accuracy and repeatability in both applications, confirming the effectiveness of the POE-based modeling and Paden-Kahan inverse kinematics. The developed platform provides a practical and extensible solution for precise robotic manipulation in modern automated production environments.

title: Dense Residual Dense Block Super-Resolution for Enhancing Vehicle Detection in Remote Sensing

Author Affiliations: Department of Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Universitas Indonesia, Kampus Baru UI, Depok, Indonesia; Department of Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Universitas Indonesia, Kampus Baru UI, Depok, Indonesia; Research Center for Telecommunication, National Research and Innovation Agency, Bandung, Indonesia

Abstract: Accurate vehicle detection in complex traffic environments remains a challenging task, particularly when dealing with low-resolution imagery and small-scale objects such as distant vehicles and pedestrians. Limitations in image quality, caused by hardware constraints, transmission noise, and real-time processing requirements, often lead to significant performance degradation in conventional object detection frameworks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an integrated super-resolution–assisted vehicle detection framework that combines a transformer-based SR preprocessing module with a YOLOv12-based object detector. The proposed SR module is designed to exploit global contextual information and long-range dependencies, enabling more faithful reconstruction of fine-grained structural details that are critical for small-object recognition. The enhanced high-resolution representations are subsequently fed into the YOLOv12 detector, which offers a favorable trade-off between detection accuracy and computational efficiency across multiple object scales. Extensive experiments conducted on multiple benchmark datasets, including VEDAI-VISIBLE, VEDAI-IR, DOTA, and xView, demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms existing CNN- and GAN-based SR methods as well as baseline detection models. Quantitative and qualitative results confirm notable improvements in detection accuracy, particularly for small and densely distributed vehicles, while maintaining practical inference efficiency. These findings highlight the effectiveness of integrating transformer-based SR as a preprocessing stage for robust vehicle detection, contributing to more reliable intelligent transportation and traffic monitoring systems.

Abstract: This paper presents a Python-based automatic reading system for circular pointer-type gauges, designed to estimate readings from a single image in natural and industrial environments. The proposed method follows a three-stage pipeline that decomposes the task into detection, structural segmentation, and text recognition. Specifically, YOLO is employed to localize the gauge region of interest, U2-Net performs multi-class segmentation to extract the gauge center, pointer, and scale marks, and PaddleOCR is used to recognize scale numerals. To establish correspondence between recognized numerals and their spatial positions, a geometric analysis pipeline is introduced, including contour extraction, radial clustering, angular mapping, and median absolute deviation (MAD)-based outlier removal. The final gauge reading is computed via angular interpolation between the pointer direction and adjacent scale values. The training set consists of 200 images from four-gauge types, while the test set includes 695 images from five-gauge types. Quantitative evaluation on 695 valid test samples achieves a median accuracy of 99.55 percent and a mean accuracy of 99.56 percent, measured using normalized full-scale absolute error. Additional qualitative experiments on web-collected and real industrial images demonstrate that the proposed approach generalizes effectively across diverse dial layouts.

title: Design-Oriented Digital Twin Framework for Optimal VSC Setpoint Synthesis in Hybrid AC/DC CIGRE Low-Voltage Networks
Authors: M. A. Kamoona; J. M. Mauricio
Author Affiliations: Department of Electrical Engineering, Universidad de Sevilla, Seville, Spain; Department of Electrical Engineering, Universidad de Sevilla, Seville, Spain
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract: This paper presents a design-oriented digital twin framework for the offline optimal synthesis of Voltage Source Converter (VSC) setpoints in hybrid AC/DC distribution networks. Eight bidirectional VSCs are used to combine a DC grid with the original AC feeders of a modified CIGRE European low-voltage benchmark. To simulate the network topology, operational limitations, and time-varying load profiles under hourly operation, the Digital Twin (DT) is implemented in Python using the PyDAE environment. An optimization problem is formulated to determine the active and reactive power setpoints of the VSCs on an hourly basis over a 24-hour horizon, aiming to minimize the power exchange at the main grid connection while strictly enforcing per-phase current limits and bus voltage constraints. Penalty-constrained Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) are used as solution methods in the DT environment to address this constrained nonlinear problem. The proposed framework operates as a design-phase virtual twin for offline parameter synthesis and robustness assessment across multiple operating scenarios. The obtained optimal setpoints are then validated under four representative load conditions, including AC-stressed and high DC-penetration scenarios. The simulation results show that the synthesized VSC setpoints successfully prevent voltage and current violations, improve power sharing, and reduce feeder overload without the need for continuous communication. A comparative analysis indicates faster convergence and slightly lower power consumption with HHO than with PSO. The proposed framework provides a reproducible and high-fidelity platform for constraint-aware optimization of hybrid AC/DC distribution grids.

title: A Low-Cost EEG Artifact-based Brain-Computer Interface for Wheelchair
Authors: D. Birthariya; J. Akbar; A. C. Nair; B. Yilmaz

Abstract: This paper presents a low-cost Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) solution to power wheelchair navigation through the detection of electroencephalogram (EEG) artifacts. Using a consumer-grade Muse 2 headset, the system captures EEG data across four channels to identify intentional ocular and muscle movements. Signal processing is performed via Welch’s method to extract the Power Spectral Density (PSD) across five frequency bands. A 34-feature vector is constructed, incorporating log-transformed power, signal standard deviation for artifact identification, and frontal/temporal asymmetry ratios. The trained classification model is exported to the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) format and deployed within a Java-based Android application. This application communicates with an ESP-WROOM-32 microcontroller over Bluetooth to command a modified hoverboard chassis utilizing 350W hub motors and custom Field-Oriented Control (FOC) firmware. To ensure user safety, the system incorporates an ultrasonic (HC-SR04) sensor array for automatic obstacle avoidance and an RFID (RC522)-based hardware interrupt for immediate toggling between BCI and manual joystick modes. The system was validated through a multi-user study involving six participants. Results show a mean individual classification accuracy of 92.2% and a cross-subject (unseen) accuracy of 86%, indicating generalization capability for real-world wheelchair navigation. Abstract: Graph embedding is a fundamental problem of mapping nodes of a guest graph into a host graph while minimizing the distance distortion, with broad applications, including virtual network embeddings into physical topologies, VLSI design, or community detection in social networks. title: Nebula: Proving Machine Executions via Folding Schemes
Authors: A. Arun; S. Setty
Author Affiliations: New York University; Microsoft Research
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
Abstract: A zero-knowledge virtual machine (zkVM) is a versatile, developer-friendly primitive that proves the correct execution of programs on a fixed machine architecture. A major bottleneck for these protocols is the prover's space complexity, which grows linearly with the number of program steps and makes it impractical to produce proofs for longrunning computations. To overcome this, we propose generating these proofs incrementally, using folding schemes. However, realizing this requires new tools in the folding setting: (1) an efficient read-write memory argument for proving the correctness of memory operations; and (2) a method to eliminate the overheads incurred by unused machine instructions when incrementally proving a program execution step. We address these with new techniques. First, we introduce commitment-carrying IVC, where a proof carries an incremental commitment to the prover's non-deterministic advice provided at different steps. Second, we show how this unlocks efficient read-write memory arguments (which implies indexed lookups arguments), with a cost profile identical to that of memory arguments in the context of non-recursive arguments. Third, we provide a new universal “switchboard” circuit construction that combines circuits of different instructions such that one can “turn off” uninvoked circuit elements and constraints, offering a new way to achieve pay-per-use prover costs. We design an IVC scheme, which we refer to as Nebula, that incorporates these techniques. We implement a prototype of a Nebula-based zkVM for the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM). We find that our techniques qualitatively provide a $30 \times$ smaller constraint system to represent the EVM over standard memory-checking techniques, and lead to over $260 \times$ faster proof generation for the standard ERC-20 token transfer transaction when compared to our baseline Nova (CRYPTO'22) with existing arithmetization methods.

title: Creating a Digital Twin RL DAA Model to Drone Flight Framework
Authors: M. Ullrich; S. Vidhyadharan; J. Hagberg; P. Snyder
Author Affiliations: John D. Odegard School of Aerospace Sciences, University of North Dakota, Grand Forks, USA; John D. Publication Title: 2026 Integrated Communications, Navigation and Surveillance Conference (ICNS)
Abstract: This project presents a Digital Twin framework for detect-and-avoid (DAA) research, training, and validation, culminating in real-world flight execution on swarm of UAVs. The system integrates reinforcement learning (RL), simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop execution to evaluate DAA behavior across representative encounter scenarios. The Digital Twin models uncrewed aircraft dynamics, sensor observations, and realistic obstacle geometries—including static infrastructure and moving traffic. These efforts emulate operations involving interactions between cooperative and non-cooperative crewed aircraft with uncrewed aircraft. Each mission produces a CSV log containing the agent’s pose, clearance, time-to-collision (TTC), and event flags; allowing any flight to be reviewed, replayed, and analyzed as needed.The research team developed an end-to-end DAA framework that trains an intelligent avoidance policy in simulation and executes the resulting flight path in a physically identical real-world environment. The system uses Crazyflie 2.0 quadcopters operating within a simulated training environment, which is a digital representation of the University of North Dakota Aerospace indoor swarm testbed at Robin Hall. All simulation, training, and telemetry data are expressed in a shared physical coordinate frame with the origin at the center of the flight area, enabling maneuvering space of ±3.15m longitudinally and ±1.475m laterally and allowing direct correspondence between simulated and real-world execution.Policy training is performed using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), implemented with Stable-Baselines3 on PyTorch. The PPO agent employs an MLP actor-critic architecture. To maximize robustness, three distinct behavioral variants were employed—Red, Blue, and Yellow; each using variant-specific entropy coefficients and learning-rate schedules. These presets allow for the systematic exploration of tradeoffs between exploration, convergence speed, and functionality. Monitoring and management of long-running training is supported through checkpointing, automatic resume, and consistent naming conventions unique to each variant. Training runs automatically save at regular intervals and support training resuming, so a multi-day training campaign never loses progress.Evaluation callbacks log mission-critical metrics including: goal achievement, collision, boundary violation, and timeout rates. These metrics are reported to the user via TensorBoard, enabling continuous monitoring of policy robustness throughout training.Central to the creation of a model capable of both stable and interoperable DAA behavior is the layered curriculum. Training progresses through multiple difficulty levels; the model is exposed to increasing stages of complexity. Agents first master low-risk navigation behaviors before advancing to timed dodge drills and increasingly aggressive challenge layouts. Regulated by these curriculum stages are maneuvering caps, obstacle density, dodge-drill probability, reward bonuses, and penalty scaling. Promotion between training stages is governed by short evaluation windows and explicit performance gates (e.g., goal-rate thresholds), while timeout-based difficulty caps allow improved time-to-goal performance to unlock additional complexity; eventually arriving at the full-complexity scenario. Because each stage has a rigidly refined performance gate, the exact point where a policy struggled can be traced where a policy struggled, allowing targeted correction.The combined RL and Digital Twin framework allows for nuanced analysis, reaching beyond simple success metrics, that may not be possible or cost-effective in hardware-only research. Per-episode telemetry provides minimum clearance, time-to-collision (TTC), maneuver latency, and path deviation measurements relevant to DAA performance envelopes. Deterministic acceptance tests and specific scenario suites support side-by-side comparison across policy variants and random seeds; while animation exports provide visual evidence suitable for pilot and safety-engineer review.The trained models are capable of detecting and avoiding both static and moving obstacles with a high reliability while reaching assigned goals without collision or boundary violation. A mission-execution wrapper allows users to specify these key locations via a command-line interface, enabling rapid scenario generation without recompilation. Each mission is first executed in simulation, producing a CSV telemetry file that is then consumed by a Python-based Crazyflie flight controller. Real-world execution uses Crazyflie’s built-in library to perform waypoint navigation with optional live plotting and configurable safety parameters, including goal radius, obstacle proximity thresholds, and speed limits. Missions conclude with automated reporting of success, collision, out-of-bounds, or timeout outcomes, followed by autonomous takeoff, path execution, and landing. Future work includes higher-fidelity sensor models (ADS-B, radar, and vision), formalized curriculum rules tied to quantitative risk thresholds for airspace authorization, and expanded sim-to-real transfer studies to assess readiness for deployment in both reserved corridors and mixed cooperative/non-cooperative airspace. The intermediary CSV creation/ingestion can also be simplified away in favor of real-time streaming of the telemetry data directly to the Crazyflie control program.

Abstract: The increasing convergence of Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) has exposed industrial control systems (ICS) to cyber threats traditionally confined to enterprise networks. While continuous network monitoring is recommended by standards such as IEC 62443 and NIST SP 800-82, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) lack the financial and technical resources required to deploy commercial OT security platforms. This paper presents Sentinela-OT, a frugal, and passive system designed to provide network visibility and unauthorized-access detection in PLC-based industrial environments. The proposed architecture combines open-source software (Suricata and Python) with low-cost embedded hardware (Raspberry Pi 5) and managed-switch port mirroring to monitor OT traffic out of band, ensuring zero interference with control operations. Detection is based on whitelist-driven identification of authorized communication endpoints, leveraging the deterministic and static nature of industrial networks to identify unapproved devices attempting to access PLCs. Real-time alerts are delivered through a lightweight Telegram-based notification interface, enhancing operator situational awareness without requiring complex dashboards or centralized infrastructure. The system was validated in a physical laboratory environment using real PLCs and industrial protocols (Modbus/TCP and Profinet). Experimental results demonstrate reliable detection of unauthorized access attempts, sub-second alert latency, and stable resource utilization on embedded hardware, with no observable impact on PLC communication performance. Sentinela-OT demonstrates that meaningful OT network visibility and access monitoring can be achieved using affordable, reproducible components, making it suitable for SMEs and resource-constrained industrial settings as a complementary layer to existing cybersecurity frameworks.

Abstract: The push for passive biometrics to mitigate hygiene risks associated with touch-based sensors has particularly increased after the COVID-19 outbreak. This paper proposes a novel system that uses the MediaPipe BlazePose framework, a system that extracts an abstract 33-landmark skeletal topology in real-time, functioning on standard CPU hardware. To ensure environmental robustness, a geometric algorithm calculates a scale-invariant biometric ratio $\left({R = \frac{{Stride}}{{Height}}}\right)$, allowing for consistent identification regardless of the subject’s distance from the camera. KineticID processes all video data in volatile RAM, ensuring no personally identifiable images are stored, making it a "Privacy-by-Design" architecture. Integration between the Python-based vision engine and an ESP32 microcontroller is achieved via the lightweight MQTT protocol, enabling physical lock actuation with sub-100ms latency. Experimental results validate the system’s efficacy as a hygienic, GDPR-compliant, and cost-effective alternative to traditional biometrics.

Abstract: The exponential growth of Internet of Things (IoT) networks demands low-power and highly reliable data transmission despite constrained energy budgets and dynamic wireless channels. This approach provides a scalable software solution for energy-aware, intelligent IoT communication and forms a foundational step toward autonomous physical-layer adaptation in future 6G systems.

Abstract: The increasing deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) in critical infrastructure has introduced a class of security risks that remain insufficiently characterised and poorly tooled in practice. This paper presents VectorSec, an open-source, web-based LLM security scanner built with Python and Dash. Abstract: Cloud task scheduling is a complex optimization problem that has a decisive influence on the use of resources, execution latency, and scalability of distributed infrastructures. This conveyed that the C-NOT QC-gate demonstrated an enhanced task scheduling with an improvement of 4.97% and 9.74% compared to the Hadamard and Phase-T gate. This research supports utilizing entanglement-based scheduling achieved using the C-NOT gate for improved and optimized latency, thus making it the most effective gate set up to schedule cloud tasks.

Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education, Krishnan Kovil, Tamil Nadu, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education, Krishnan Kovil, Tamil Nadu, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education, Krishnan Kovil, Tamil Nadu, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education, Krishnan Kovil, Tamil Nadu, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education, Krishnan Kovil, Tamil Nadu, India

Abstract: Maintaining hygienic conditions in domestic and commercial kitchens is critical for food safety, yet hygiene inspections are largely manual, making them time-consuming and error-prone. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes SmartVision, an automated kitchen hygiene monitoring framework that integrates deep learning-based visual inspection with Internet of Things (IoT) sensing. The system uses a NodeMCU (ESP8266) microcontroller connected to an ultrasonic sensor for waste-level monitoring, a power sensor for appliance usage tracking, and a buzzer for alert generation. A Python-based vision module employs a YOLObased model to identify hygiene violations such as spills, cluttered surfaces, unclean areas, and overflowing waste bins from real-time images. Sensor data and visual detection results are transmitted via Wi-Fi and displayed on an LCD for real-time feedback. SmartVision provides a low-cost, scalable, and modular solution for home kitchens, restaurants, and institutional food-preparation environments. By combining visual intelligence with sensor-based monitoring, the system reduces reliance on manual inspections while improving hygiene compliance and kitchen safety.

Abstract: The use of autonomous systems to increase productivity, lessen reliance on manual labor, and reduce operational errors in material handling has increased due to the quick development of industrial automation. In order to accomplish these goals, autonomous industrial vehicles, or AIVs, are essential because they make it possible for dependable cargo transportation in factories, warehouses, and other semi-structured settings. Robust navigation and adaptive decision-making, however, continue to be major obstacles, especially in busy and dynamic industrial environments. A computer vision-based framework for autonomous industrial vehicle navigation and decision-making is presented in this article. The suggested system uses camera-based perception to create depth maps, identify obstacles in real time, and extract road masks and uses this data to generate Bird's Eye View (BEV) maps to calculate safe routes, prevent collisions, and improve navigation by combining adaptive decision-making algorithms with image processing techniques. This article presents a computer vision-based framework for autonomous industrial vehicle navigation and decision-making. The proposed system generates depth maps, detects obstacles in real time, and extracts road masks using camera-based perception. title: Coordinated Dual-Layer Management of BESS and Volt–VAr Control in Active Distribution Networks
Authors: R. R. Biazzi; D. P. Bernardon; M. Sperandio
Author Affiliations: Center of Excellence in Energy and Power Systems, Federal University of Santa Maria, Santa Maria, Brazil; Center of Excellence in Energy and Power Systems, Federal University of Santa Maria, Santa Maria, Brazil; Center of Excellence in Energy and Power Systems, Federal University of Santa Maria, Santa Maria, Brazil
Publication Title: IEEE Access
Abstract: This paper proposes a dual-layer coordinated framework that combines day-ahead battery energy storage system (BESS) scheduling with real-time Volt–VAr Control (VVC) for active distribution networks. The optimization minimizes distribution system technical losses while satisfying operational constraints related to voltage regulation, equipment loading, battery operation, voltage regulator (VR) tap commutation, and smart inverter (SI) operating limits defined by IEEE Std 1547-2018. The planning stage determines the optimal charging and discharging schedule of multiple BESS units over a 24-hour horizon, whereas the operational stage performs real-time VVC through the coordinated control of VRs, capacitor banks (CBs), and SI associated with distributed photovoltaic (DPV) and BESS units. The methodology was implemented in a Python–OpenDSS co-simulation environment and validated on a modified IEEE 34-bus feeder using real SCADA load measurements and solar irradiance data through daily and seasonal operating scenarios under both planning and actual operating conditions. Performance was also compared with conventional local VVC strategies. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework maintains voltages within prescribed limits, eliminates or substantially mitigates reverse power flow, reduces feeder peak demand, and significantly decreases network energy losses. Overall, the proposed strategy significantly enhances the operation of active distribution networks with high renewable energy penetration.

The system includes an automated Blood Network which provides emergency situations with quick access to suitable blood donors for emergency needs. Users complete a personal profile when they register. The section contains demographic details which include blood type and age and current health status and lifestyle indicators and location. The system uses its geo-intelligent matching engine to find nearby donors who match with the required criteria during emergency situations. The system provides an efficient method to establish contact between donors and recipients. The system comprises AI inference pipelines together with automated report creation and database functions which utilize location data for their operations. Image data is processed locally on edge devices and stored in a cloud-based MySQL database, enabling daily growth tracking and predictive harvest estimation. Unlike traditional monitoring methods that require manual labor and exposure to agrochemicals, our system significantly reduces health risks for field workers and increases phenotyping accuracy. title: Structural Connectivity Modeling With Graph Curvature Features for Brain Tumor Analysis
Authors: S. R. Dip; H. K. Meena

Abstract: This work presents a low-power field-programmable gate array-based biomedical sensing system for early detection of brain tumors using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). While MRI is a key medical sensing modality, existing deep-learning-based diagnostic methods are computationally intensive and unsuitable for real-time resource-constrained sensor platforms. To address this challenge, a graph signal processing framework is proposed that models MRI pixel intensities as graph signals, enabling effective representation of the non-Euclidean spatial connectivity inherent to the MRI sensing process. Ricci curvature is employed to characterize local structural connectivity variations and tumor-induced asymmetries through curvature-driven graph features. The proposed sensor-aware framework is explicitly designed for edge-deployed MRI sensing systems and is implemented on a Python productivity for Zynq UltraScale+ (PYNQ-ZU) FPGA platform to demonstrate measurable improvements in sensing-system efficiency. Experimental results on the BR35H and Kaggle-253 datasets achieve classification accuracies of 96.50% and 91.94%, respectively. The system requires only 0.0011 million parameters, achieves an inference latency of 3.85 seconds per image, and consumes 0.33 joules per inference, demonstrating its suitability for real-time energy-efficient medical sensing applications.

title: Deep Learning Models for Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting: A Comparative Study with Multi-Horizon Predictions
Authors: M. Taktak; A. Fakhfakh; F. Derbel
Author Affiliations: Smart Diagnostic and Online Monitoring Leipzig University of Applied Sciences, Leipzig, Tunisia; SM@RTS Laboratory, Digital Research Center of Sfax, University of Sfax, Sfax, Tunisia; Smart Diagnostic and Online Monitoring Leipzig University of Applied Sciences, Leipzig, Tunisia
Publication Title: 2026 8th Global Power, Energy and Communication Conference (GPECOM)
Abstract: Real-time high-precision short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is critical to enable smart grid operation, improve energy efficiency, and maintain stability of the power system. However, the majority existing studies focus on forecasting accuracy while neglecting real-time operational constraints and requirements. This paper presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of 5 deep learning architectures which include LSTM, GRU, CNN-LSTM, Bi-LSTM, and RNN for a prediction of 15 to 60 minutes based only on historical power generation data. The comparison is carried out on real data from a rooftop PV installation in Leipzig, Germany, the models are compared for accuracy, inference speed, and uncertainty quantification. The results demonstrate that LSTM achieves superior accuracy in all forecast horizons (RMSE: 72.85 W at $15 \mathrm{~min}, 92.55 \mathrm{~W}$ at 60 min). CNN-LSTM delivers competitive performance with $\mathbf{7 0 \%}$ fewer parameters and the lowest horizon degradation $\mathbf{(2 1. 5 \%}$ vs 27.0% for LSTM), making it the most balanced architecture for practical deployment. Experiments on a Raspberry Pi 400 reveal that inference speed differences observed on desktop hardware vanish on edge devices, where the overhead of Python and the framework dominates computation. The practical differentiator for edge deployment is the model size: CNN-LSTM (453 kB) and Simple RNN (406 kB) require roughly three times less storage than LSTM (1.4 MB), which makes them better suited for resources-constrained devices.

Abstract: Inefficient parking management is a major problem in smart cities, which leads to the congestion of urban traffic. The simulated experiments in Python and MATLAB on a synthetic smart-city parking dataset indicate that the ASPS has a 63.4 percent decrease in the average search time, a 71.2 percent enhancement in system throughput, and a 48.7 percent decrease in end-to-end latency as compared to traditional cloudonly solutions. Abstract: In this paper, a predictive overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) monitoring system in the context of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has been implemented. The proposed OEE monitoring system aims to solve the different problems like latency, the lack of real-time visibility, and human error in the OEE measurements. The proposed OEE monitoring system is based on the implementation of a Python-driven hardware-in- the-loop (HIL) simulation environment and the development of a three-tier processing architecture using MQTT communication protocols. The proposed OEE monitoring system is also based on the implementation of a dual-model artificial intelligence (AI) framework using Isolation Forest and LSTM neural networks for anomaly detection and predictive fault forecasting, respec- tively [10], [11]. Furthermore, the authors proposed a predictive Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) workflow that allows the automatic generation of 5-Why reports in 30 seconds after the occurrence of any fault in the IIoT environment. Abstract: The research introduces a methodology to predict the flexural behavior of a laminate before conducting any experimental tests. More specifically, a Random Forest regression model was trained to identify the nonlinear behavior associated between the laminate stacking sequence, the fiber properties, and its flexural response, based on the flexural test dataset. To practically implement this AI–predictive approach, an interactive, real-time interface was set up via a Python package, Streamlit, a tool that can be used to visualize flexural strength and deflection under different stacking sequences. In this way, both laminate material selection and experimental design can be more efficiently informed. In addition to visualizing flexural performance metrics, this approach allows the identification of the important features based on the model's feature-importance functionality. As part of this study, mechanical testing was also conducted on various hybrid laminates ([K/G/C/C/G/K], [C/G/K/K/G/C], and [G/C/K/K/C/G]) and non-hybrid laminates ([K]₆, [G]₆, [C]₆). title: Latency-Aware Speaker Identification in Browser Environments: A Comparative Study of Lightweight vs. Deep Architectures

Abstract: Speaker recognition using machine learning that is accessed through a web-based user interface (UI) utilizing server-side inference faces strict limitations on both latency and usability; Users expect feedback in nearly real-time and do not want to have to download or install anything, while there are still limits to how much computing power and memory can be used. We examine how classical and deep learning techniques can be utilized to achieve low-latency speaker recognition within a browser-accessed application utilizing server-side inference where training data is limited. To accomplish this we implemented 5 different models utilizing the same audio preprocessing pipeline and train/test split, and also implemented a common timing harness: A Multilayer Perceptron (Neural Network), a Support Vector Machine (SVM), a Random Forest Classifier, An AdaBoost Classifier, and an X-Vector-inspired embedding network. All of the latencies stated were determined at the server-side Python inference only; End-to-End Latency will require the additional latency associated with a network round-trip, serialization, and client-side JavaScript runtime. Our results indicate that classical models provide the best speed – accuracy trade-off: The SVM achieved a 95.0% test accuracy with an 8 ms server-side inference time, and a 120 KB model size, While the Random Forest Classifier achieved an 85.0% test accuracy with high cross-validation performance (CV Mean = 90.5%). Our results indicate that the embedding network underperformed many of the classical baselines and had longer inference times and larger model sizes than many of the classical baselines. These results suggest that lightweight classical models are competitive with, and may be preferable to, deep learning based models for responsive, browser-accessed speaker recognition systems where the amount of enrollment data is limited.

Abstract: Dynamic edge networks suffer from fluctuating bandwidth, latency, and edge-node load, which weaken conventional task offloading strategies under deadline and energy constraints. This study proposes an adaptive task offloading strategy based on dynamic network states. An online broad learning system predicts short-term bandwidth, transmission delay, and load from sliding-window observations. The predictions are embedded into a model predictive control framework for rolling optimization of the local-edge task allocation ratio, while confidence-interval-guided compensation adjusts decisions under prediction uncertainty. ADMM is used for distributed solution. NS-3/Python simulations show that the proposed method achieves a $93\%$ task success rate, 1.22 W average terminal energy consumption, 3.2 switches/s, and 45 ms average completion time, outperforming local execution, reactive offloading, and DQN-based offloading. The proposed strategy improves real-time reliability, energy efficiency, and robustness in highly dynamic edge computing environments.

Abstract: With the rise of deceptive job offers, financial scams, and grooming on platforms like Reddit, safeguarding users against social engineering threats has become increasingly critical. High-risk subreddits in this study were defined as communities that have been reported or observed to facilitate activities such as online grooming, human trafficking, exploitation, fraudulent recruitment, and other forms of malicious social engineering. Abstract: This paper constructs a collaborative optimization model involving the edge, cloud, and end-user, integrating communication, computing, energy consumption characteristics, and task latency constraints. Addressing the shortcomings of existing algorithms, such as susceptibility to local optima and poor adaptability to dynamic scenarios, this paper proposes an original algorithm for joint scheduling using Adaptive Weighted Chaotic Eagle Optimization-Deep Q-Network (AW-CHAEO-DQN). The algorithm improves the Eagle Optimization algorithm through adaptive chaotic mapping, optimizes the initial weights and sampling strategy of DQN, designs a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism to adapt to changing scenarios, and employs dual-timescale scheduling to balance global optimization and real-time decision-making. Abstract: Visual Speech Recognition (VSR), or lipreading, is a method of understanding a person’s speech through observing the movements of their lips, as opposed to hearing them speak. This fully visual form of communication can help people communicate effectively with one another who are deaf or who have hearing challenges, or it can enable the creation of systems that provide a command interface in an environment that is entirely silent. Mudra is a complete, end-to-end VSR system developed to predict a spoken word from a standard video camera and 500 different words in a vocabulary. Our VSR implementation is designed around a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that uses images from cropped video frames of the subject’s mouth to extract spatial features in order to predict the spoken word. These spatial features are then passed to a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network so that the Mudra system can understand the timing and flow of the individual’s lip movements over successive frames. Before the model sees a video, we first process the video to (1) perform face detection automatically, (2) create and define 2D facial landmarks, (3) align the face with the mean shape, and (4) generate a 96 × 96 pixel patch of the center of the mouth in grayscale at a rate of 25 frames per second. We trained and tested this entire process using the Lip Reading in the Wild (LRW) dataset, which contains more than 500,000 video clips with over 500 distinct words. Due to the weight of a model containing 500 words, we also created lighter models of 10 and 20 words for usage in specified instances. We packaged the project into a functional web application with a React front-end and Python FastAPI back-end, allowing users to simply upload a video and receive real time predictions. Our testing indicates that the CNN-LSTM pipeline can perform comparablely to the LRW dataset, which shows that we can create practical speech recognition systems that operate without the need of microphones.

Abstract: The fast emergence of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) necessitates the deployment of lightweight and secure authentication algorithms to safeguard healthcare information that is sensitive. Abstract: This paper presents the complete design, physical implementation, and software-stack integration of a dedicated Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) that executes a high-precision Hindu astronomical calendar (Panchang) computation engine on the GPDK 90 nm CMOS node. Conventional ephemeris algorithms are computationally expensive and energy-intensive, which makes them unsuitable for wearable and IoT edge platforms. We propose a hardware-accelerated micro-architecture that combines a four-lane vectorized fixed-point datapath (Q16.16) with a dedicated time-window comparison (time_window_compare, TWC) block to evaluate the four primary Panchang elements—Tithi, Nakshatra, Yoga, and Karana— in a single clock cycle while delivering sub-arcsecond (~0.055″) longitudinal precision. The design is taken through a complete RTL-to-GDSII flow using the Cadence EDA tool-chain with clean DRC/LVS signoff. The accelerator occupies a 220×175 µm core (0.038 mm2) at 72% utilization, operates at 50 MHz, and dissipates 42.5 mW of total power (post-synthesis estimate, VDD = 1.0 V, typical-typical corner, 25 ◦C). A companion Python/Flask backend and an Android frontend demonstrate end-to-end deployability. Against a documented software baseline running on a Raspberry Pi 4B platform, the ASIC achieves ~250× latency reduction and ~28× power reduction, enabling offline, real-time Panchang generation in smartwatch-class form factors.

Abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication offers high data rates and inherent spatial security, but its directional nature poses significant challenges for mobile platforms such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). This testbed provides a flexible and open framework for researchers to prototype and evaluate advanced UAV-based mmWave communication strategies, including machine learning–driven beam alignment, neighbor discovery, and secure link acquisition. Abstract: This study investigates the use of machine vision technology and computer simulation algorithms to analyze the dynamic characteristics of spinning table tennis trajectories. A comprehensive technical framework is developed by integrating high-precision motion capture, physics-based numerical simulation, and statistical data analysis. In the experimental system, machine vision is used to automatically track the flight and rebound processes of the ball. High-speed cameras operating at 1000 frames per second capture detailed motion information with a spatial resolution of 0.1 mm, enabling accurate extraction of key trajectory parameters, including landing position and rebound height. The simulation module is based on a six-degree-of-freedom dynamic model that incorporates aerodynamic drag, the Magnus effect, and collision mechanics. An explicit Euler scheme is used for time-domain discretization, allowing real-time iterative updates of the ball motion state with a time step of 0.001 s. A Python-based data processing pipeline is further developed to synchronize machine-vision measurements with simulation outputs. Rather than treating the visual tracking results only as one-way validation data, the framework establishes a two-way feedback mechanism for jointly identifying the coefficient of restitution and the tangential friction coefficient, thereby improving the physical consistency of the simulation model. Experimental validation was conducted under controlled conditions across spin intensities ranging from −1550 to +1550 RPM, with more than 300 trials performed. Statistical analysis based on five repeated tests for each spin condition shows a mean relative error of 4.3%, a standard deviation of 2.1%, and a 95% confidence interval from 3.2% to 5.4%. The systematic and random components of the error are 2.7% and 1.9%, respectively, while the previously reported worst-case error below 8% corresponds to the upper decile of the observed error distribution. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective computational tool for quantitative trajectory analysis and physics-based model calibration. However, its current contribution lies primarily in experimental measurement and simulation validation, rather than direct training support, which would require further human-subject experiments and application-oriented evaluation.

Abstract: Assessing graduate students’ academic performance is a multifaceted task that requires consideration of both quantitative metrics and qualitative evaluations. Abstract: This paper examines the idea of combining 5G Radio Access Network Quality of Service measurements, which are Quality of Service Class Identifier and Channel Quality Indicator, alongside artificial intelligence to automatically adjust billing. In contemporary business implementations, customers become dissatisfied with the network performance that is below the expected standards with the use of a static billing system. Using a dataset of 414 different measurements of network performance, this study suggests an autonomous model that links real-time signal soundness and charging triggering signals to the financial system. Abstract: With recent developments of high-resolution satellite imaging, a wealth of information has been made available in the Earth observation. Hence, it is necessary to use proper methods that will automatically detect the trend in land-use and surface characteristics as it is unfeasible to examine huge volumes of satellite images manually. The given task is often not easy to perform using standard methods of machine learning because the spatial structure of remote Sensing data are often intricate. This project is aimed at tackling these challenges with the help of a deep learning solution that relies on the ResNet-18 convolutional neural network for image classification. The model makes use of transfer learning, whereby it uses the parameters of a network that has been trained on ImageNet data to initialize the network, and the analysis of satellite images is then finetuned. The dataset used to conduct the performance evaluation is the EuroSAT dataset and the classified images of the different land-use areas, including the agricultural areas and urban areas. The system is constructed on Python Torch and supplemented with the use of Adam algorithm to speed up the process of training. title: A Web-Based Preprocessing Pipeline System for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data Fusion
Authors: L. Liu; Y. Xiao; R. Huan; Z. Shi
Author Affiliations: School of Automation, Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou, China; College of Environmental and Resource Sciences, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China; School of Automation, Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou, China; School of Automation, Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou, China
Publication Title: 2026 14th International Conference on Agro-Geoinformatics (Agro-Geoinformatics)
Abstract: Multi-source remote sensing data synergy enhances the spatiotemporal coverage and information richness of land surface observations. However, inherent differences among sensors in spatial resolution, radiometric calibration, spectral response functions, and observation geometry introduce systematic biases that must be resolved through preprocessing before joint analysis. The necessary steps include geometric correction, atmospheric correction, cloud masking, terrain correction, bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) normalization, and cross-sensor radiometric harmonization. In current practice, this workflow remains reliant on offline scripts or manual operations, with low efficiency and limited reproducibility. Existing cloud platforms (e.g., Google Earth Engine, PIE-Engine) offer general-purpose computing environments or configurable workflow builders, requiring users to construct processing chains or write code. To our knowledge, few Web-based systems have been specifically designed to encapsulate the complete preprocessing-harmonization-fusion workflow into parameterized, configurable nodes for multi-source data fusion. This paper presents such a system, with Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province as the study area, providing a configurable, traceable, and programming-free unified platform. The system adopts a layered architecture with decoupled frontend and backend. The presentation layer (React, Ant Design) provides form-based parameter configuration and real-time task monitoring. The service layer (FastAPI) implements a database-driven workflow with SQLite, where each processing step stores intermediate products and metadata in dedicated tables and front-end filter options map directly to SQL queries. An asynchronous task queue supports background execution with progress polling. The algorithm layer encapsulates Python remote sensing modules (GDAL, NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch) behind a unified interface, supporting dynamic loading and tile-level parallel scheduling. Adding a new processing node requires only defining a database table, implementing an entry function, and registering the task type. The system is demonstrated through a multi-source remote sensing preprocessing-harmonization chain as the core business instance. The chain comprises six standardized nodes - geometric correction, atmospheric correction, cloud masking (FMask for Sentinel-2, spectral-index-based for HJ-2/GF-1), Sun-Canopy-Sensor (SCS) terrain correction, BRDF normalization, and cross-sensor radiometric harmonization via a Fourier Feature Transformer (FT-Transformer) - that unify surface reflectance from multiple sensors to a comparable baseline, yielding temporally consistent and radiometrically comparable fused datasets. This framework is not restricted to specific sensor combinations. To validate the system, multi-source data from Hangzhou were processed end-to-end from raw imagery to fused products through the web interface. Results demonstrate stable operation across all modules with correct scheduling and feedback. Band-wise comparisons and quantitative error analyses against reference imagery confirm that the preprocessing-harmonization chain substantially reduces radiometric discrepancies among multi-source data, yielding mean absolute errors below 0.04 in reflectance units across visible and near-infrared bands, with vegetation index MAE below 0.06. This system elevates multi-source preprocessing and fusion from script-based, fragmented processing to an integrated platform for multi-source remote sensing data fusion.

Abstract: This paper presents an integrated platform of an SDR-based RF detection (NI USRP-2932, NI LabVIEW 2018), GPS anti-spoofing geolocation (u-blox NEO-M8N, Python), and real-time GIS mapping (Folium, OpenStreetMap) within a single unified pipeline, constituting Phase 1 of a two-phase validation study. Abstract: Understanding how neural networks develop emergent behavior remains one of the main challenges in computational neuroscience. Models that balance the dynamics of microscopic ion-channels with macroscopic behavioral responses are important, but most strategies have lost cellular details in favor of network scale. OpenWorm c302 (302 neurons, 7000 synapses) and implementation of ModelDB (ModelDB 266796), a model of the human hippocampal circuit with healthy and epileptic variants, provide complementary advantages: connectome topology and complete neuronal physiology, respectively. This study offers a hybrid structure, which combines the hippocampal ModelDB-based biophysics with the network topology of c302, to allow real-time voltage propagation, synaptic co-ordination and temporal synchronization via Python-based cross-framework communication. Electro-physiological properties and locomotor emergent behaviors are reproduced in the hybrid simulation. The benchmark tests indicate a great correspondence with experimental results: AVA inter-neuron peak firing rate of 34 Hz (target 32-35 Hz), VB motor neuron synchrony index of 0.87 (target  $\ge 0.85$ ) and 96% correspondence in the sequences of body-wall muscle activation. The hybrid system maintains fine-grained neuronal fidelity and has realistic coordination on a network scale compared to stand-alone simulations of c302 or ModelDB. The condition of adaptation modulation of the synaptic weights and ion-channel conductance produces stable and non-saturating oscillatory dynamics. The hybrid system establishes a two way communication between the hippocampal and C. elegans neural models to study how biophysical and whole-network dynamics can interact to produce emergent behavior. The model combines a comprehensive model of neuronal dynamics with fully connected brain regions, which has led to research on how localized neurons processes can lead to complex organisms.

Abstract: This paper presents a methodology for developing end-to-end simulations of direct-to-chip two-phase cooling systems for high-power data centers using a coupled Flow Network Modeling (FNM) and Digital Twin platform. AI workloads executed on high-performance GPU servers are transient and spatially non-uniform, leading to time-dependent and uneven heat dissipation across GPUs, servers, and racks, which places significant demands on cooling system design. As rack power density increases, the physical footprint of single-phase liquid cooling systems—driven by high flow rates, large pipe diameters, pumps, and heat rejection equipment—becomes a limiting factor. Two-phase cooling systems, by leveraging evaporation and condensation, offer significantly higher heat transfer capacity per unit mass flow, enabling reduced flow rates and more compact cooling infrastructure. However, in two-phase cold-plate-based systems, pressure drop and flow distribution are strongly coupled to local heat absorption due to phase change, resulting in thermal–hydraulic behavior that is substantially more complex than that of single-phase flow networks. To address these challenges, the Flownex™ Simulation Environment is extended through the development of a dedicated two-phase component library for data center applications, including models for cold-plates, flow loops, manifolds, heat exchangers, and coolant distribution units (CDUs). In parallel, the FNM simulator is integrated into a Digital Twin platform developed in Python and connected to the NVIDIA Omniverse™ Kit through the USD framework, enabling real-time visualization, live data streaming, and interactive user control. This paper focuses on the methodology, modeling workflow, and software architecture required to develop the two-phase library and deploy system-level cooling models within an interactive Digital Twin environment.

Authors: J. Rajendran; H. S. Pillai; D. Rajesh Kannan Megalingam
Author Affiliations: Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham; Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham; Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Humanitarian Technology (HuT) Labs, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham
Publication Title: 2026 International Conference on Smart Futuristic Technology
Abstract: Health care is shifting very fast to wearable and portable medical devices like ECG monitors, pulse oximeters, and glucose meters. Such devices enable continuous real-time monitoring and quick diagnosis. Unfortunately, these are powered by low-power microcontrollers that have limited computational resources, thereby making it difficult to deploy large ML models. Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) makes it possible for AI models to function in such limited devices effectively by pruning and quantization. Nevertheless, in case the biomedical signals are complicated, TinyML may still face challenges in maintaining the required speed and energy efficiency.This work presents a simulated FPGA accelerator that supports TinyML models for healthcare IoT devices. The FPGA unit is the one that handles the parallel operations, thus, inference is getting faster and the device is becoming more energy-efficient. Performance metrics like latency and power are being measured through PYTHON analytics simulation and hardware-aware optimization.The theoretical investigation of the topic indicates that the adoption of FPGA-style acceleration can lead to a huge efficiency improvement when compared to CPU-only TinyML execution.
Author Keywords: TinyML;FPGA;Healthcare IoT;ECG;Low Power;Software Simulation
IEEE Terms: Field programmable gate arrays;Modeling;Tiny machine learning;Electrocardiography;Hardware;Internet of Things;Quantization (signal);Energy;Simulation;Printing

title: Deepfake Audio Detection using Self-Supervised Speech Embeddings and LSTM/BiLSTM Network
Authors: P. M; A. A; M. V; P. K. R
Author Affiliations: Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Nandha Engineering College, Erode, India; Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Nandha Engineering College, Erode, India; Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Nandha Engineering College, Erode, India; Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Nandha Engineering College, Erode, India
Publication Title: 2026 6th International Conference on Inventive Computation and Information Technologies (ICICIT)
Abstract: Recent developments in the domain of speech synthesis and voice conversion have led to a proliferation of extremely realistic audio deepfakes, threatening people's privacy, media credibility, and cybersecurity. In this paper, a simple yet effective framework named Generalized Deepfake Audio Detection (GDFA) is presented. The proposed GDFA framework employs self-supervised speech-based embedded representations (SER), a two-stem splitter (TSS), and a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network. Through the use of self-supervised speech models, high-level phonetic and contextual features of deepfake speech are learned. The TSS method helps separate vocal formants from other noises in speech to improve the distinction of genuine and artificial voices. The framework has shown outstanding detection performance on the Fake-or-Real database when evaluated based on a BiLSTM model while being designed for low computational cost and real-time applications using an interactive Python web application (Streamlit). While recognizing its limitations in achieving cross-dataset detection performance, the proposed GDFA framework offers an extremely effective solution for digital forensics and media authentication purposes.
Author Keywords: Deepfake Audio Detection;Artificial Speech Recognition;Self-supervised Speech Representation;BiLSTM;Two-stem Splitter
IEEE Terms: Modeling;Deepfakes;Signal detection;Speech;Printing;Bidirectional long short term memory;Equations;STEM;Spectrogram;Timing

title: Digital Twin-Assisted Intent-Driven Autonomous Virtual Network Function Orchestration Using Federated Intelligence for Resilient 6G Networks
Authors: K. Golla; M. Ramkumar
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Saveetha School of Engineering, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Saveetha University, Chennai, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Saveetha School of Engineering, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Saveetha University, Chennai, India
Publication Title: 2026 4th International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
Abstract: The 6G networks require autonomous and smart management of resources to support ultra-dense devices, dynamic traffic and low-latency services. The classic methods of Network Function Virtualization (NFV) orchestration utilize primarily the use of either a static or heuristics algorithm, which constrains their capacity to adjust to the dynamically evolving network conditions. Additionally, the current digital twin and distributed learning systems are characterized by a high level of synchronization overhead and poor automation abilities. To cope with these issues, this paper suggests a Federated Intelligence-based Digital Twin-Assisted Intent-Directed Autonomous Virtual Network Function (VNF) Orchestration. The proposed methodology combines the idea of digital twins to represent a real-time network with the idea of federated learning so that one can train models using a set of distributed edge nodes and maintain data privacy. In Python, the machine learning model is applied to interpret the network traffic data and forecast the demands of resources to be efficient in the orchestration of VNF. The experimental findings indicate that the suggested framework with such a high prediction precision of about 98, a higher usage of resources and a lower latency rate. The paper concluded that incorporating digital twins and federated intelligence could be useful in future 6G networks management to achieve high degrees of automation, scalability, and resilience.
Author Keywords: Digital Twin Networks;Federated Learning;Network Function Virtualization (NFV);6G Networks;Autonomous Network Orchestration

title: A Multimodal Framework for Human–Robot Collaboration Using Egyptian Arabic Speech and Hand Gestures
Authors: M. N. Bayoumi; M. Y. Halim; M. I. Awad; S. A. Maged; M. Elshalakani
Author Affiliations: Mechatronics Engineering Department, Faculty of Engineering, Ain Shams University, Cairo, Egypt; Mechatronics Engineering Department, Faculty of Engineering, Ain Shams University, Cairo, Egypt; Mechatronics Engineering Department, Faculty of Engineering, Ain Shams University, Cairo, Egypt; Mechatronics Engineering Department, Faculty of Engineering, Ain Shams University, Cairo, Egypt; Mechatronics Engineering Department, Faculty of Engineering, Ain Shams University, Cairo, Egypt
Publication Title: 2026 8th International Youth Conference on Radio Electronics, Electrical and Power Engineering (REEPE)
Abstract: Human–robot collaboration (HRC) has become increasingly important in industrial and domestic environments; however, many existing systems provide limited support for Arabic-speaking users and suffer from reduced reliability under noisy conditions. This paper presents a realtime multimodal interaction framework that integrates Egyptian Arabic speech recognition with static hand gesture recognition for intuitive control of an ABB IRB 120 robotic arm. Speech commands are processed using the Python Speech Recognition library with the Google Web Speech API, while ten predefined static hand gestures are recognized using MediaPipebased landmark extraction and classified through a Support Vector Machine (SVM). To enhance robustness and ensure continuous interaction, an automatic switching mechanism enables seamless transition from speech-based control to gesture-based input when voice commands fail. Experimental evaluation under ten different background-noise conditions shows speech recognition accuracies exceeding 95% for most commands, while the gesture recognition module achieves an average accuracy of 96% during real-time operation.
Author Keywords: Human-robot collaboration (HRC);Multimodal interaction;Egyptian Arabic speech recognition;Hand gesture recognition;Robotic arm control
